c: In the name of God the Father Almighty and of His only-begotten Son Jesus Christ, and of the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit. We, the Twelve Apostles, ministers of His only-begotten Son Jesus Christ, being gathered together in one place in Jerusalem, the city of the great King, and with us our good and holy brother Paul, the Apostle of all the Gentiles, and James, the brother of our Lord, who is the bishop of this city of Jerusalem, have ordained this right doctrine, and have appointed degrees of offices for the Church, according to the pattern of that which is in heaven; and we charge each one of you severally, with thanksgiving for that our Lord Jesus has called us to His glory. The bishop is in the likeness of the shepherd of the sheep, and the presbyter in the likeness of a teacher, and the deacon as a minister, and the sub-deacon, behold, he is as the same; and the reader also, and the skilful singers... and the rest of the people as those who hearken to the word of the Gospel, and, moreover, understand the word of admonition. For thus have we ordained the law for the Church, (even) this book of admonition, which we have written, and have sent with Clement, our ministering brother, into the world, that men may walk according to the commandment of the Churches which are under heaven, and may have perfect understanding, that, when they have heard these commandments which are written therein, they may find life eternal, honour and glory from our Lord Jesus Christ, who has bestowed on us this mystery which is from Himself. But those who keep not His law shall be cast into the fire which is not quenched, and their abode also shall be in the fire of Gehenna for ever, as it is written.

But apostles and presbyters and all the people, who have believed in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and work righteousness and peace, shall find compassion and mercy from God the Father, the Ruler of the whole world, and His Son Jesus Christ, and shall come to knowledge of Him in the Holy Church of God. And those who serve Him shall be a pure and elect vineyard, and shall find life eternal by this faith, and victory by the Holy Spirit; and shall be strong by the power of Jesus Christ and the faith of Him who has redeemed them by the sprinkling of His holy and precious blood, and has bestowed on them the privilege that they should call on the Almighty, that He should be their Father and their God and their Friend, and that they should be fellow-heirs and joint-partakers of His Holy Son. Hearken to the holy admonition, you who receive at the commandment of our Saviour the words of the Gospel and His glad tidings.’ which is full of glory.

O you children of God, keep His commandments and do His will; but if there be anyone that seeks to follow after sin and that does all things that are not pleasing to God, he shall be numbered with those who transgress His law and His commandment. And now I say to you, keep far from injustice and oppression, and desire not to take for yourselves the portion which is greater and (to leave) to your neighbour the less. For it is written in the law, saying, ‘You shall not desire your neighbour’s wife, nor his field, nor his man-servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor anything; none of the possessions of your brother,” nor anything like thereto; it is adultery. But if there be anyone who desires to do thus in the lust of his heart, he shall be far from God, (even) our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be glory with His Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever. Amen. For He teaches us and gives us understanding and strengthens us by the Holy Spirit, that He may fulfil the law, in which it is written, saying, ‘You shall not commit adultery, but I say to you, everyone who has looked upon a woman and lusted after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.” And he also who desires to do thus shall be condemned with the adulterers. And, behold, he that thinks in his heart, and desires to take unjustly his (neighbour’s) ox, or his ass, or his field, and continues so to do, shall be numbered with the adulterers. For the prophet says, “Woe to them that join house with house and unite field with field, and hedge with hedge, that they may take what is not theirs.” And again it is said, Know you who dwell on the earth that this word was heard in the ears of the Lord of Sabas.” And in another place also it is said, “Cursed be everyone that steals his neighbour’s landmark, and the people shall say, So be it.” Wherefore Moses says, ‘Desire not your neighbour’s landmark and take not away the law which your fathers ordained.” Because of these things come fear, and death, and trouble; and judgment from God shall find those who do thus. But such as hearken to the word of God, and keep His glorious law in faith, shall find compassion and mercy. For it is said, “What you hate for yourself, do not to your neighbour.” And as you do not desire that any other should look upon your wife to lead her astray in sin, so likewise do not you look upon the wife of another with evil thoughts. And as you do not desire that another should take your garment, so likewise do not you take the garment of another. And as you do not desire for yourself cursing, and reproach, and beating, so likewise do not you thus to your neighbour. But if there be anyone who has cursed you, do you bless him; for it is written in the Book of Numbers, Blessed be those that bless you, and cursed be those that curse you.” And, moreover, it is written in the Gospel, Bless them that curse you, and pray for them that oppress you; and do good to them that hate you, and render not evil to them that oppress you, but bear with them patiently.’”" For the Scripture says, “Take not vengeance on your enemy for the evil which he has done against you; and for this cause ‘the Lord will help you, and bring judgment upon your enemy.” For it is said in the Gospel, “Love your enemies, and pray for them that persecute you, that you may be the sons of your Father who is in heaven, for he makes the sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and unjust.”, Beloved, let us understand these commandments, that we may be sons of light.

Bear patiently with one another, O you sons of God. And let the husband also bear patiently with his wife, and not be haughty or false; but let him he merciful and upright, and cherish her alone in love and humility. And let him not take pleasure in, nor desire, another woman, lest she lead him astray to evil. But if you commit adultery, and doest thus, you shall surely dic, and the wrath of God shall come upon you; and you shall be condemned with a bitter condemnation. But if you think evil in your heart, and commit not‘! adultery with her, it shall be sin to you. And if you have prepared and adorned yourself, that the wife of your neighbour may love you, you have erred and have become a stumbling block to her, and made her to commit adultery. And for this cause condemnation shall come upon you, for God says, “You shall not desire,” and “You shall not commit adultery.” For you have led her astray to love you by the beauty of your youth, and by the charm of your face, and for this cause you have become a partaker with her in the work of sin and your curse. Wherefore it is meet that you should pray to the Lord your God, that all this sin find you not out. But you ought in purity to please God, that you may find rest and life eternal before God. For it is said, Let not the hair of your head grow long, but cut (it) and purify yourself, that you may serve God and not be separated from Him. But do not you anoint yourself with perfumed ointment, nor clothe yourself with gorgeous apparel to lead women astray, nor yourself, nor become an occasion of sin, but seek purity and well-doing. And you, O man of God, let not the hair of your head grow long; plait (it) not, nor curl (it), for all this is a sign of impurity and adultery. For it is written in Deuteronomy, “And you shall not put on a garment which is woven with wool and flax: you shall make for yourself a twisted fringe for your garment.” But we ought not to shave our beards, nor to change the nature of man into another fashion.

And if you do thus, you are a trans ress law and far from God, who created wah His men and His likeness. But if you desire to please God, do no evil, and put far from you all that your God hats And be not a drunkard, and walk not in the streets with the adulterers without wisdom and knowledge, but labour and live by the work of your hands; and seek to do all that is pleasing to God; and remember the word of our Lord Jesus, and follow Him at all times. For the Scripture says, “And who reads his law day and night; whether in the way, or in the house or while you sleep, love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your mind and with all your strength,” that you may find from Him compassion and mercy.

But if you are rich, and have no need of the art and labour of your hand, with which to earn your bread and livelihood, be not slothful, nor sit idle, but go to the faithful, and sit with them, (even) with them that are united with you in faith; and speak with another of the word of life, and read what is in the Book of Kings and the Prophets, and sing a psalm of praise, and hearken to the word of the Gospel, which is the fulfilment of the whole law.

And keep far from all service of the gods of the Gentiles; and take no heed of any words of vanity which profit not, and seek no other law, nor false prophets who change and corrupt the faith. What then are you unable (to find) in the law of God, that you should seek after the learning of the Gentiles? But if you desire to know the power of the interpretation of the Scriptures, seek out the Book of Kings: and if you wish to find out the power of the wise and their teaching, you have the prophets, Job and Solomon. These are they that are full of wisdom, and you shall find knowledge in them. These, more than all teachers, shall make understanding to increase, for their word is the voice of the Lord God, who alone is all-wise. And if you desire a song, you have the Psalms of David. And if you desire to seek to understand the creation of the world and the generation of the first fathers, you have the Law.’ And if you desire to know wisdom and doctrine, you have the book of the law, which is full of the glory of the Lord God. Keep far, then, from works of evil, and from the doctrine of Satan, and the word of vanity, which is not in the law; but read what is in Deuteronomy, that you may understand and know the glory of God, who has saved you from many snares of Satan. For the Saviour came not to destroy the Law and the prophets, but to fulfil them, and to loose the bonds which are in Deuteronomy, and to bring men to a spiritual teaching. Wherefore He calls us, saying, “Come to me all you that are troubled and heavy laden, and I will give you rest.”' And you, when you have read the Law and the prophets and (the Books of) the Kings and the Gospel, shall understand how many were the righteous men who have reigned and pleased God in their lives, and for this have found life eternal; and also you shall know how many evil kings have transgressed through lack of understanding. These have perished and been destroyed by the stroke of the judgment of God,’ and have lost eternal life. And knowing this, you shall be strong in the right faith, and shall find grace and favour with our Lord Jesus Christ, for you are one of His members.

Moreover, when you desire to bathe, enter not into the bath where the women bathe, lest they see the beauty of your youth, and the charm of your flesh, and stumble because of you, or you yourself sin and fall by reason of them.

snare of her lips, and he followed her in the wicked blindness of his heart.” And furthermore it is said, “Look not on an evil woman, for honey flows from the lips of an adulterous woman, which for a time is sweet to your throat, and afterwards you shall find it more bitter than gall, and sharper by far than a two edged sword.” And again it is said, ‘Keep your way from her, and draw not near to the door of her house, lest you give your life to others, and your livelihood to them that are without mercy; lest strangers be filled with your strength, and your labour pass to the house of another; and you shall repent afterwards when your flesh (and) your body are weakened, and you shall say, How have I hated instruction, and my ears are turned from reproof, and I have not hearkened to the voice of them that gave me commandments,” who admonished me and taught me, nor caused my ear to attend: I have been nearly in all evil.” And now also I say to you, Choose out all the good things which are written in the Holy Scriptures, that we may not neglect these witnesses,?” and turn aside to a multitude of words, but may be strong in faith, and in doing good. And let us keep far from all evil-doing, and be pure from all evil (and) uncleanness before God, that we may find life eternal.

Let the wife obey and be subject to her husband, for “the head of a wife is her husband,” and the head of the man that walks in the way of righteousness is Christ; and “the hea Christ is God” the Father, who is above all, ene and is to come, the Creator of all, with His Son our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be honour, greatness, and majesty and glory. You women also obey your husbands, and be in subjection with humility and honour and the fear of God; and delight your husbands with good Service, that you may find favour with them, as we said before. For thus says the wisdom of Solomon, “If any man have found a brave woman, she is more precious than a jewel of great price. She that is such, the heart of her husband trusts in her; she that is such-, good spoil will not be wanting. She helps her husband with good in good, and not with evil in evil (in) her life; who cards wool and flax, (and) has wrought with her hands (that which is) good. She is as a ship which trades afar; and she gathers for herself all riches. And she rises up by night, and gives food to her household, and their tasks to her handmaidens. She saw a field and bought (it); with the fruit of her hands she planted a possession. She firmly girded her loins, and put forth her hands to the work. She tasted that labour is good, and her lamp goes not out all night long. She stretches out her hands to what does profit, and her arm is strong to spin. And she opened her hands in mercy to the needy, and the palm of her hand is stretched out to the poor. And her husband has no care about his house, even if he terris long anywhere. All her household are clothed;' double cloaks of fine linen and purple she made for her husband, and for herself she made garments. And her husband becomes notable in the gates, when he sits in the assembly" with the elders of the land. Linen garments she made, and gave (them) away, and girdles for the Canaanites. And her mouth she opened according to the law, and set a fence for her tongue. With strength and beauty was she clothed, and rejoiced in the latter days. They that enter her house are many: she has not eaten the bread of idleness. She opens her mouth in wisdom, and according to the ordinance of the law; and her almsgiving has brought up children and enriched (them), and her husband has praised her. Many daughters have obtained riches,’ and many have done mightily, but you excel and have surpassed them all. Flattery is deceitful, and beauty is despised, for a wise woman shall be blessed, and she that fears the Lord shall be extolled. Give her of the fruit of her lips, and let her husband be praised in the gates,” that you, O women, may know that a woman who loves her husband: shall find honour and blessing and compassion with the Lord God. Take heed and understand, O woman, that desire and wish to be faithful, that you may please the Lord, not yourself, nor adorn yourself for another man; and clothe not yourself with gorgeous apparel, nor put sandals on your feet for show, as the harlots do to lead (men) astray: but keep yourself from all evil-doing and adultery, lest by you other men offend. Obey your husband rather, and show kindness to him. But if you desire to walk about in the assembly and the streets, to ensnare the souls of many, then judgment from God shall come upon you, and you shall be as one that has no hope, as when a wicked man falls into great affliction, and brings on himself disgrace, and dishonour, and sorrow. In like manner a wicked woman brings on herself dishonour: and as,a lion that lies in wait and rends, so she ensnares fools, even as it is written, saying, “As moths (destroy) a garment, and as decay a tree, so sorrow wastes the heart of a man.” And furthermore it is said, “It is better to dwell in the wilderness, than that you should dwell with a quarrelsome and talkative and passionate woman." And now also I say to you, O Christian people, look not after nor follow adulterous women. But it is right for faithful women to veil themselves in purity, not seeking to enhance the beauty of their faces with dyes and painting and adornment, which have no profit, on the form which God created. Let them not do thus, but when they walk in the way let them incline their heads, being veiled.

And take heed to yourselves, you faithful women, and speak no (word of) hate to anyone, but above all (not) to your husbands. O you good and gentle women, worship God with joy and gladness; and you also, our children and our brethren and kinsmen and beloved, seek after the precious wisdom that adorns our life, and enlightens our -hearts, and brings us close to God, and wins for us an entrance into the Kingdom of heaven in life eternal and rest.?

Of bishops we have heard thus from our Lord Jesus Christ, that the shepherd of the sheep who is ordained bishop of all the Churches must needs be blameless, pure and good, who thinks not on the care of this world, who is full fifty years old, who has passed the strength of youth, who is not a slanderer, nor one that speaks lies amongst the brethren. For the Gospel says, “lor every word that a man speaks thoughtlessly, he shall give account in the day of judgment, that it may condemn him.’” And furthermore it is said, “l’or by your words you shall be justified, and by your words you shall be condemned.” Wherefore it is meet that he abound in all good things. But if he be not learned, let him be prudent and intelligent, of middle age. But if the city be a small one, and there be not found therein one (thus) fitted for the office of bishop and there be found among the young men one prudent and wise, though his years are (but) few, and if those who know him bear witness that he is worthy to be ordained bishop, if he have lived from his youth perfect in the works of the holy and humble fathers,’ and walks in the way of righteousness, tried in every work, and if (men) bear witness to him that he is perfect, let him be ordained in peace. For Solomon also when but twelve years old became King over the people of Israel; and Joash too became ruler when he was seven years old and afterwards in the eighth year he reigned in righteousness. For the Lord spoke by the mouth of Isaiah the prophet, and said, “To whom shall I look, but to him that is meek and humble and quiet, who trembles at my word?" and again it is said in the Gospel, “Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.” Let him therefore be merciful, for it is said, ‘Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.” Let him therefore be a peacemaker, for it is said, ‘Blessed are the peacemakers; they shall be called the children of God.” Let him be pure of heart, without revenge and evil and unrighteousness, for it is said, Blessed are the pure in heart; they shall see God.”

fit., Let him, then, be spiritual, and watchful to do good, neither insatiable nor passionate, nor a drunkard, nor vindictive, without hatred and strife, not haughty, nor a lover of money, nor a neither let him exalt himself, lest he fall into the snare of Satan; for everyone that has exalted himself shall be abased, and he that humbles himself shall be raised to honour. And let such a one be ordained bishop who has married one elect wife, who is able to order his household aright, a teacher and monitor who has brought up his children in purity. And let his wife also be faithful, who trains her children in the true worship and in the fear of the Lord. It is right that the men of his household should obey the bishop in humility and in fear, and let him be master even as it is written.

And let them try him that he be blameless, not passionate, (for) thus says wisdom, Anger destroys the wise man.” And let him be merciful and charitable, for our Lord says, “And by this shall all know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.” fit., Let him, then, be a lover of men, who receives strangers, who accepts not persons, a man of understanding, who shows favour neither to rich, nor to poor, one who has a craft,” whose hands are open to give, who receives widows, a lover of the poor and the orphans and widows. And moreover let him support those (widows) who have children. But if there be a slothful man, or one who has spent all his substance in drunkenness and fornication, and desires to receive alms, let not the bishop show any care for him, nor permit him to enter the church. For the Scripture says to those who act thus, How long will you lic, you and when will you awake from sleep? A while you sleep, and a while you sit; a while you slumber, and a while you fold your hand to your breast; and then as an evil messenger comes poverty upon you, and want as a swift) runner.”

It is not right for the bishop to judge, accepting the person of the rich, and to neglect the poor. Tor God said to Moses, Judge not, accepting the person of the rich, nor turn aside the judgment of the poor, for the judgment is the Lord’s.” But he ought to judge up rightly. The food of the bishop ought to be food seasoned with moderation, that he may be able to teach and admonish the people, and that he may turn them to God. And let him keep far from all evil, and read the Scriptures at all times and be a lover of wisdom, that he may be able to interpret the Scriptures in the Holy Spirit, (even) the words of the Gospel, the Law and the prophets. The Lord?’ says, “Understand you the words of the Scriptures, for they bear witness of me.” It becomes a bishop to search out and expound the Scriptures in order, and to satisfy the people with spiritual teaching, and fill them with the light of the law of God with much admonition. God says, “Make the light of wisdom to shine upon you, for it is time.”

Thus, then, it is right for the bishop to suffer and toil and wrestle for righteousness sake, but above all before the people, that they, when they see his works, may receive his admonition. And, moreover, let him become surety for no man, nor associate with the great, nor be of a double tongue, nor follow after princes, but let him fear God; and let him not hearken to a false accusation against his neighbour. And let him not be slothful in fasting, nor seek occasions for eating, nor say, To-day is a feast, as the Gentiles do, to eat and drink and be wanton: but let him remove from him every idle desire which has no profit, for all this is despised and hateful before God, and well-pleasing to demons.,It is meet for the bishop to command and admonish the people to remove from them all these works. But let him teach them and turn them, that they may imitate him and follow (him) in righteousness. [or God said to the children of Israel, ‘Observe my law and my commandment.” And Jesus Christ Himself also, our Lord and our God, first did all, and (then) taught us to imitate Him. Wherefore He says that he who shall teach and do, shall be great in the Kingdom of heaven.? It is right for you, O bishops, to teach the people and save them from error, even as Christ has given you grace. For the Lord spoke by the mouth of Ezekiel the prophet, and said, ‘Son of man, have made you a watchman to the house of Israel, and you shall hear the word from my mouth, and admonish them by my word. When I say to the sinner, You shall surely die, and he has not repented, and you have not spoken to him, nor admonished him, that he may repent and turn from his (evil) way and live, that sinner shall die in his sin, and his blood will I require from you, says the Lord. But if you have admonished the sinner, and he has not turned from his sin, he shall die in his guilt and you shall save your soul.” And if the righteous man has turned from his righteousness and committed sin, while I show him punishment before his face, and you have not admonished him, he shall surely die in his guilt, and his righteousness which he has done I will not remember, and his blood will I require from your hand. And if you have admonished the righteous man, so that he sin not, that righteous man shall surely live, and you also have saved your soul.” ‘As when war and strife arise in the midst of a people, and they seek out a watchman to bring them tidings, that they may be on guard, and if he tell them not beforehand, that they may be saved from defeat, their blood shall be upon his head, for they heard not the sound of the trumpet. But if he see the sword which comes on the land, and blow with the trumpet a signal to the hosts, and (if) one who hearkens hear the sound of the trumpet and get him not away, and the sword come and find him, his blood shall return on his own head, for he heard the sound of the trumpet, and gat him not away, and his blood shall be poured out on him; but he who gat him away saved his life.” In like manner the bishop, if he teach the word of life, shall find life eternal.‘ The sword is eternal condemnation, and the sound of the trumpet is the Holy Gospel, and the watchman is the bishop of the Holy Church. The bishop ought to feed (the flock), and teach, and hold fast the word, and make men to fear concerning the judgment. Wherefore let him admonish those that walk without knowledge, and make them to see plainly; and let him teach those that know not, and confirm those that know; and let him gather those that are lost and speak to them at all times concerning their salvation, that, when they hear these things, they may be admonished and do (that which is) good. For God says by the prophet, “Testify against this people, and tell them their sins (to see) if they will turn, and repent, and be saved from their iniquity.” And Moses also said to the people, “Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one.” And again, it is said in the Holy Gospel, ‘“‘He that has ears to hear, let him hear.”

And Solomon also says, Hear, my son, the instruction of your father and disregard not the commandment of your mother.” Yet they have not heard to this day, but have forsaken the Lord the only true God, and He has called them a generation of transgressors and adulterers, concerning whom we have spoken before.

And now know, beloved, you who have been baptized into the death of our Lord Jesus Christ, that it is not meet that they should sin who have received such grace as this. Know, brethren, that such as these who, after they have received baptism, turn back to deeds of sin, shall go down to the condemnation of Gehenna.

And (there are) others also who have not been believers, but (who) afterwards when they have believed and been baptized become blessed before God, even as our Lord says in the Holy Gospel, “Blessed are you when they revile you and mock you, and speak all (manner of) evil against you falsely for my sake. Rejoice, for great is your reward in heaven.” And if there be anyone against whom they have spoken," blessed is he. For it is written, saying, ‘Every man who is not tried, is not elect before God.” there be any man who has transgressed the law, and men curse him, he has brought the curse on his own head. In like manner we also, if we hear not the commandments of God and do not His will, shall bring a curse upon ourselves, and moreover shall be far from God. For as for such as do not what they themselves teach, and turn not from their own ways, the bishop ought to admonish them, and put to shame those who do thus. But it is right that he teach them in the love of Christ how they ought to serve.;

It is right for the bishop to seek after righteousness, and not honour transgressors, nor be partial in judgment, nor take a bribe from any man, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise, nor turn aside a right cause. And moreover it is said somewhere, “Put away all evil from you.” And Solomon also says, ‘Come not into the place where they encamp; withdraw from them, and turn away. For they sleep not, unless they do evil. Sleep is taken away from them, and they sleep not who feed on sin.”

and should order their manner of living, as is fitting, in peace; that the people may lead good lives and turn from their sins. This then is well-pleasing in God’s sight, for when a man turns from his sin and returns to repentance, others seeing him are taught the true service.

Therefore ought the bishop to be watchful to do good, that the beauty of his life may be known to all; for he is the guide of the people, and the shepherd of the elders and rulers and teachers, and of all who are under him.

It is right for the bishop to turn the people to the knowledge of God, and to receive the repentance of those who have turned to God, (and) to teach them, and console them in meekness and in love and in humility, and with joy of heart; for the Lord God is merciful. For He says by Ezekiel the prophet, “Say to them,’ as I live; says the Lord God, I desire not that the sinner should die,’ but that he should repent, and forsake his evil way: and why will you die, house of Israel? When I speak to the righteous, if he trust in his righteousness and commit sin, all his righteousness I will not remember to him: in his sin which he has committed, he shall dic. And if I say to the sinner, You shall surely die, and he repent of his sin and do justice and righteousness, and return the pledge of his debt and restore what he has robbed, and walk in the ordinances of life, and commit not sin, he shall surely live, and shall not die in his sin that he has sinned, neither will remember to him his sin and his iniquity; for he has done justice and righteousness, and by it he shall live.” Wherefore sinners shall hope; when they turn from their sins and repent, they shall find a good hope; and they shall inherit the earth.

But let them that have not transgressed take heed lest they fall into affliction and sorrow and weeping. Know, then, and understand, O man, if you transgress and commit sin in this world, and repent not, you have not life. Repent, then, while you live, for after death there is no repentance. Even as David says, ‘For there is none in death who remembers you, and in Sheol who will confess to you?” It is right, then, brethren, that we should be ready to do good, and should walk in the way of righteousness, in which there is no sorrow. Let us hear, then, and understand that which is said, Direct my way and my going according to your word.” And let us not be wanting in any good work, but observe the holy word which the Holy Gospel says concerning the five wise virgins, and not (be) as the five foolish virgins, whose oil of good works failed, and they went forth from the marriage which is in heaven. Wherefore we ought to take heed to ourselves and fashion ourselves, and mark the time of the bridegroom, lest we fall into sin; but he that does righteousness let him take heed to do good even to the end. It is meet, then, that the bishop be of understanding and judge up rightly, for the judgment is the Lord’s. Let him admonish sinners, that they may walk in the right way; and, when they turn, let him receive their repentance in compassion and in mercy. Remember, then, what our Lord says, “There is great joy in heaven over one sinner that repents.”

But if you receive not them that repent, but reject them, you have scattered your flock, and have not understood what David says, ‘Deliver not to the wild beasts the soul that confess to you.” For thus says the Lord, “That which has fallen, shall it not arise and that which has erred, shall it not turn again? Wherefore has my people transgressed with an evil transgression, and held fast to their own counsel, and refused to leave it? Hearken now and hear me. Say they not thus? Is there not a man that repents of his evil, and says, What have I done? Turn again, O my children that are far away, and I will heal your wounds.” Receive them that turn to you and repent, O bishop, and be not you of a double heart, nor make proud your heart as those who have no mercy. For he who does thus fears not God: but let him rather take thought to fulfil the needs of the people, as it is fitting. Let us take heed, then, to ourselves, and have no fellowship with sinners and wicked men who do thus. The righteousness of the righteous (shall be) for himself, but he that commits sin without law, his iniquity shall return on his own head. For it is said by Ezekiel the prophet, “If a land sin against me, and go astray, and transgress, and I lift up my hands against it, and break the strength of bread,’ and send famine against it, and destroy from off it man and beast, if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should not save (it) by their righteousness, says false … have you.
they shall be saved.

the Lord God. And if send evil beasts against and upon that land, and punish it, and destroy it, and there be none left to go about (therein) because of those beasts, even if these three men were in it, as I live, says the Lord God, they shall not save their sons, nor their daughters, but they alone shall be saved, and the land shall be destroyed.” As it is written, “If ‘there be in this world a righteous man and a sinner, the righteous shall not perish with the sinner.” But He sends rain on the good and the evil. And if there be anyone who thinks and says, Judgment is equal against all, it is not so; for in this warfare there is one that is strong, and again, there is another who is stronger than he: and he that has conquered shall receive the crown of victory openly. For God condemns not the righteous with the sinner. Noah was not swallowed up in the waters of the flood: and Lot was not burnt in the fire: and Rahab the harlot perished not. But if you desire to know what happened amongst us: Judas Iscariot perished, though he was together with us in one ministry; and Simon the sorcerer received the seal of the Lord; (yet) because these two were evil, their wickedness was made known openly. Judas hanged himself, and Simon flew up (into the air) and was dashed upon the ground. And while Noah was in the ark with his sons, Ham by his wickedness brought a curse upon his children. And by this we understand that the fathers are not punished for the sin of their children, nor children for the sin of their fathers. And this thing is quite manifest, that wives are not condemned for their husbands, nor young men for their wives, nor servants for their masters, nor masters for their servants, nor kinsmen for their kinsmen, nor friends for their friends, nor sinners for the righteous, nor the righteous for sinners, but to each one is rendered according to his deeds. For Noah was not recompensed for the sin of the people, was not consumed in the fire of Sodom for the sake of Jericho, nor the children of Israel for the sake of the Egyptians. We ought not to follow the steps and the works of the and the unjust and murderers, who seek i men of hatred, who are ‘ready to shied deci a everyone shall be requited according to his works, even as David says, “For you will requite everyone according to his works.” Therefore it is right that we should help the afflicted, and visit the sick and convert the sinners, who have been wounded by deeds of sin. Let us teach them and instruct them with the word of admonition, that they may be saved from the death of sin. For it is not the whole who need a physician, but the sick; since our Father who is in heaven desires not that one of these little ones should perish. Amen.,
But do you put your trust in God and order the people as is fitting. And let not the son magnify himself against his father, nor the servant against his lord, ree. eee as violence and. words.

nor the disciple against his master, nor the official against the king, nor the layman against the bishop. For the teacher ought to have no fellowship with the disobedient and the wicked, for the sinner desires not the word of admonition. Ezekiel the prophet says, “As I live, says the Lord God, they shall no more speak this proverb in Israel. For the soul of every man is mine; as the soul of the father so the souls of his children are mine. The soul that sins, it shall die. But the man that does righteousness and uprightness, and has not eaten upon the mountains, nor lifted up his eyes to the thoughts of the house of Israel, and has not defiled his neighbour’s wife, nor come near to a woman in her uncleanness, nor done his neighbour violence, and has returned the pledge of his debt, and has not extorted, nor oppressed, and has given of his food to the poor, and has clothed the naked with his garment; and has not lent his money on interest, nor taken (anything) unjustly; and has turned his hand from sin, and has done judgment and righteousness between a man and his neighbour, and has walked in my commandment, and has kept my law, and done righteousness, he shall surely live, says the Lord God. And if he beget a son (who is) a sinner and a murderer, and does wickedness and walks not in the way of his righteous father, but has eaten on the mountains, and has defiled his neighbour’s wife, and oppressed the poor and needy, and has plundered and wrought injustice, and has not returned the pledge of his debt, and has turned his eyes towards idols, and committed wickedness, and has lent on interest, and robbed (his neighbours) and taken that which was stolen, such a one shall in no wise live, in all this sin of his which he has committed, he shall surely die, and his blood shall

return on himself. And if he beget a son, and he see all the sin of his father that he commits, and fear, and do not likewise, and have not eaten upon the mountains, nor lifted his eyes towards the thoughts of the house of Israel, nor defiled his neighbour’s wife, nor oppressed any man, but have returned the pledge of his debt, and have not robbed (his neighbours) nor plundered, but have given of his food to the hungry, and clothed the naked with his garment, and have turned his hand from wrong, and have not taken interest or bribes wrongfully, but have done righteousness, and walked in my commandment, he shall not die in his father’s sin, but shall surely live for ever.’ But his father, if he oppress, and plunder, and commit injustice,' and defraud, and do what should not be done in the midst of my people, shall die in his iniquity. And you say, Why is the son requited for his father’s sin? Because the son is righteous and has given alms, and kept my law and done (it),' he shall surely live. And the soul that sins, it shall die. But the son shall not be requited for the sin of his father; the righteousness of the righteous (shall be) upon him, and the sin of the sinner on him. If the sinner turn from his sin which he has done, and keep all my law and my commandment, and do righteousness, and (give) alms, he shall surely live, and shall not die; and all his sin which he has done I will not remember to him, but in his righteousness which he has done he shall live. Do I at all desire that the sinner should die, says the Lord, (and not) rather that he should turn from his evil way and live? But you say, It is not right. When the righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits sin, he shall dic in his iniquity which he has done. And if the sinner turn from his sin which he has done, and do righteousness and uprightness, such a one has kept his soul; and has seen, and turned from all his sin which he has done; he shall surely live, and shall not die. And the house of Israel says, The way of the Lord is not right. Is not my way right, O house of Israel? Is it not your way (which) is not right??? And for this will I judge all of you according to your way, O house of Israel, says the Lord God. Turn, and repent of your evil, and let not the punishment of your sin come upon you. Put away from you all your evil and your iniquity and your sin which you have sinned against me; and make you a new heart and a new spirit; and why will you die in your sins, O house of Israel? For I desire not that you should in any wise dic, says the Lord God, but that you should repent and live.”

See then, my beloved brethren, the greatness of the mercy of the Lord our? God, (who is) good and righteous and a lover of men, merciful and compassionate to He delights not in those that judge deceitfulness of heart, without mercy; but (wills) that one should convert and receive those Pace into the true religion, that they may be able to come to repentance. And if bishops do not teach, and act thus a will require: at their hands the sin of the people, wer as Isaiah says, “Admonish my people says God. You priests also speak to the heart of the people, and if there be any that jaded negligent as touching the sin of the people i to disregard the desire of those who seeker cance lest by his slackness the flock of the Lord perish. For concerning them God spoke by the mouth of Jeremiah the Prophet, saying, Many shepherds have destroyed my vineyard, and defiled my portion, and have made my portion, which I love, a desert and a waste; and it has become a desolation and a ruin: for my sake all the land has perished and is destroyed.”

… You also, if you see one that sins, command the deacons to expel him and put him forth, and to admonish him and teach him,’ that others, when they see, may fear. And when he turns, and comes to repentance, ict them ask, and entreat for him with God, and with the bishop, that he may teach him.” For the Saviour prayed for sinners to His Father, even as it is written in the Gospel, ‘Father forgive them," for they do what they know not.” And then let at examine him that has sinned, whether he Seal: his evil way, and when he confess his sins, and turns to repentance, let them suffer him to we the Church, and bid him to fast according to the greatness of the sin he has commits, two weeks, or three weeks, or five weeks, or seven. It is right that you should teach the sinner, and instruct him, and admonish him, without anger or favour, that he may humble himself, and pray to God, and find compassion and mercy when he stands before Him.' For it is said, “If you, O Lord, should mark sin, O Lord, who should stand before you? For forgiveness is from you,” and mercy is in your hand. Thus, then, do, and make a difference. For God said to Cain, ‘You have sinned: be silent then,” and lift not up your hand. But it is right for the sinner to grieve and and despise himself. Let us understand the word which God spoke to Moses concerning Miriam, “If her father had spit in her face, should she not have been ashamed seven days? Let her remove outside the camp for seven days and then let her enter in. And removed outside the camp for seven days, and the people journeyed not until Miriam was purified. And after this they journeyed.” Let us do, then, thus to those who desire repentance for their sins. Let us appoint for them a fixed time of years, according their sin, wherein they shall repent, let us receive them, even as fathers do their children. But if bishops, and others see on them any defilement or stain, and the people are put to shame; and (if) the judge not up rightly for the orphan, and the sors and the widow, but show favour in judgment that the may get gifts and bribes, such shall be reckoned a with the hypocrites. Even as it is written in the Gospel saying, Why behold you the mote that is in your neighbour's eye, and see not the beam that is in yours own eye? Let bishops and priests then give heed that there be not found with them deeds of this sort,- lest others be offended, when they see these evil doings. For the wicked seek occasions to destroy others and to scatter the Lord’s flock. For a little leaven much meal. In like manner sin follows after those that commit it, (and) thus destroys very many. As when a thief is found in a treasure-house and brings an evil name on his by the evil of his doings; and as when the stinking flesh of a Corpse is cast into ointment, the odour of the fragrance thereof is tainted; and as when a king is evil and cruel (and) dispenses not justice, so, too, are his princes; and as when a scabby sheep feeds with (other) sheep, they all become scabby, if it be not separated from them; and as, when a mad dog bits all whom it meets, except it be killed, all those whom it bits become mad together with it; in like manner if any man be a and a mocker, and contentious and a transgressor of the commandments which are in the law, let him be put forth from the Church, lest he corrupt the house of the Lord, and make (it) a den of robbers. It is not right that we should keep silent concerning sinners and wicked men, but we should admonish them, that they may forsake their doings, and put from them wicked deeds and habits. On the other hand, let us bid them fast and pray and give alms, that they may learn the fear of God. For He said to the children of Israel, ‘Fear me, and keep my commandments.” The bishop ought to show anxious care concerning the sin of the people, and consider the life of each one of them, that he may be to them a guide and a saviour to works of righteousness, that they may be prepared for God, and be saved from the condemnation which shall fall on sinners at the day of judgment. But let such as are slothful hear what is said, Wherefore have you kept silent concerning transgressors and gathered their fruits?

It is right that the bishop should feed the people in peace; those that have not sinned let him not suffer to fall: and those also that have sinned let him turn to repentance. Hear, O bishops, what the Lord says to you, “Despise not one of these little ones.” But they ought to forgive and pardon him that has sinned. And when a sinner confess his sin, and cries to the Lord from the depth of his heart, humbling himself with tears and sighs, the Holy Spirit will come and say to him, The Lord pardon‘! you all your sin. Know, then, O bishop, how much honour and glory God has bestowed upon you, and has given you authority to loose and to bind.‘? Take heed to yourself, and guard the flock of Christ. Walk in the way of righteousness, whilst you live in this world, for you shall give account in the day of judgment. “For to whom much has been committed, of him shall much be required.” For there is no man that lives even one day without sin, except One, who for our sakes became man, God the Word. And for this reason has been written the memorial of the ‘righteous who gave good heed to themselves. For it is said, ‘My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me, and I give to them eternal life.” And He answered the people and said to them, “Behold, I judge between rams and sheep. Know, then, that you have fed in a good pasture; and the rest of the pasture you have trodden with your feet … my sheep have eaten.” And again, ‘Now shall you know that I am the Lord, and you are my sheep, the sheep of my pasture: you are my sheep and I am the Lord your God, says the Lord.” Hear, you bishops, and hear, you people, what God says, Behold I judge between rams and he goats.” Moreover He says, “I will give judgment against the shepherds of the sheep who have destroyed my flock by their And again He says, “I will judge between bishop and bishop, between peoples and peoples, between ruler and rulers.” And my sheep are rational creatures, and are not without reason; and therefore let not the people say, We are sheep and not shepherds, what is this to us? Wherefore it is right that we should keep far from evil and deceitful shepherds who spare not, nor save the flocks, but follow the good shepherds who spare and save their flocks.

For the people love a good shepherd, and fear him as a father, and a lord, and as a priest, and as God’s high-priest, for he admonishes them, and guides them to true godliness. For he that obeys him, has obeyed Christ, and heard His voice, but he that rejects him and hears not his voice, has rejected and transgressed against Christ,’ as he that obeys Christ, has obeyed God. Moreover it is said, ‘He that hears you, has heard me, and he that rejects you, has rejected me, and he that rejects me, has rejected him that sent me.” In like manner it is right for the bishop to love the people as his children, for they are his sons; and to nurture them with admonition as a bird which broods over her eggs, and nurtures her young ones until they fly. In like manner let him teach the people the word of God, and feed them with spiritual doctrine, and give what they need to all who desire to receive of him; and let him not be burdensome to them, but admonish them with words of wisdom, and put them in fear, lest they turn again to sin. Rather let him bid them walk in the way of righteousness, and keep the faith; and let him feed the people in peace. Moreover let him raise the fallen, and strengthen the weak, and gather together the scattered, and heal the wounded in heart, and console the faint-hearted, and strengthen the lame with the word of admonition; and let him lighten the heavy burden of their sin, that they may get them a good hope. And as for them, let them learn the law of the Church, and turn to repentance. And if there be any man who is cast out through not understanding the words of the Scriptures, despise him not, nor suffer him to fall into sin, but help him, and heal him from the wound of sin, and turn him to you, and restore him to the Christian flock. But whoever refuses to turn again, he shall go forth from your flock, and be made food for the birds of the heaven and the beasts of the field; and his portion shall be with them that, say, Let us eat and drink: to-morrow we die; and that think not on their latter end. And if there be any man whom the bishop has seen doing thus, he ought to say to him, I will bear your sin, and die in your stead, even as Christ died for the sin of the world. Then let him toil and suffer with him, until he turn again to repentance. Kor “the good shepherd gives up his life for the sheep; but the hireling who is not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, sees the wolf coming, and flees and leaves his sheep, and the wolf catches them and scatters them. Because he is a hireling, he cars not for the sheep.” It is right that we should know that God is merciful, and desires not the death of a sinner, but his conversion and return to repentance. And if there be anyone that sins through understanding not the commandments which God has ordained for repentance, but walks in the deceit of his or and remembers not his sin, and his evil which he hat done, remembering not the words of the Holy Scriptures which have proclaimed mercy to him, such a one shall perish and be without hope. But search you out a good shepherd, and a meek and patient teacher and monitor, and one that is merciful and a peacemaker, who goes about and feeds his sheep, and seeks that which is lost, like the Lord our God. For our Father who is in heaven sent His beloved Son our Saviour the Good Shepherd, our Teacher Jesus Christ, who left the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and went to seek one sheep that was lost. And when He found it He bore on His shoulder,’ and brought it to the flock with joy, because He had found that which was lost. Hear this, O bishop, guide them that have gone astray, and gather together them that have been scattered, and seek them that are lost, for you have authority to turn (to repentance), that you may bind and loose. For our Saviour” said to the man with the palsy, “I have forgiven you your sin; your faith has saved you; go in peace.” For the peace which we have received is the Church of Christ, where into you should bring them that have repented of their sins and are cleansed," and have done righteousness and goodness, and found the hope of life. The bishop ought to heal the sick who are diseased through deeds of sin; to visit them and to console them and to heal their wounds, for “not the whole, but the sick are they that need the physician. For the Son of man came to seek and to help that which was lost.” Since then, you are a physician in the Church of the Lord, impart healing to each one as it befits, and feed them with spiritual food, that they may be strong in the Holy Church. And feed the flock of Christ in humility and in love, and mild severity without anger, not exalting yourself in your position of authority, for you are the shepherd of the sheep of Christ’s flock; and you shall gather the lambs in your bosom.

Be, then, merciful and just, without guile or revenge, or jealousy, or slandering, or calumny or hatred, or partiality, or evil speaking, or haughtiness or boasting. Despise not them” that are under you, nor hide from them the commandments of God, nor turn yourself away from their repentance, nor bring pretexts against them, nor drive them away from the Church. Be of understanding, then, in judgment, and receive not the witness of one man against any, but only the witness of three good and faithful men,' to whom others bear witness that they are good and faithful, who cherish not hatred, nor revenge, nor jealousy. lor there are some that speak falsely, that have two tongues, or three, who rejoice in evil-doing, haters of the brethren, who seek to scatter the flock of Christ. But if you hear their voice, and believe those that do thus, behold you have scattered your flock without judgment, and given them over to evil and ravening wolves, that is (to) evil men. Or rather, they are not men, but evil beasts who are in the likeness of men, ungodly and unbelieving and apostates, who know not God. Such are liers in wait in the way, and like a wolf that seizes and devours, they seize them that depart from the law of the Church; and when they see one that is lost, it seems a great thing for themselves. For their father, the devil, is a murderer. And those that go astray from the Church, and depart from the law, devils shall be their shepherds, and shall afflict them with torment and distress and sorrow of heart. And they shall follow the way of transgressors, and shall lose their reward, and shall depart farther and farther from God. And as for the bishop, if he judge not up rightly, his portion shall be with them.’ You ought not, then, to thrust away the sinner, nor to despise him that turns; neither be you lacking in mercy, that you may heal the wound of sin, nor have you fellowship with the man of blood. For concerning them the Scripture says, Their feet are swift to shed blood; shame and affliction are in their way, and they know not the way of peace; and there is no fear of God before their eyes.” The way of peace is our Saviour Jesus Christ, who has taught us, saying, Forgive, that he may forgive you; and give, (and) men shall give to you;” that is to say, Forgive men their trespasses, that your heavenly Father may forgive you your trespasses. Moreover He has taught us in the Prayer, saying,! “Forgive us our trespasses and our iniquity as we also forgive him that has trespassed against us.” But if you cannot forgive the trespasses of him that has trespassed against you," how shall you find forgiveness for your trespasses And if there be anyone that has been thrust forth being innocent, and then returning has asked for pardon, and (the bishop) receive him not, he is a murderer of his brother, and a shed der of blood like Cain, who shed the blood of Abel his brother; and his blood cried to God. And if any bishop thrust forth (a man) being innocent, he is, like Cain, a murderer.

For he that thrusts forth an innocent person, is worse than a murderer, and perceives not the mercy of God, for he remembers not the love of his neighbour.'’ And he who does thus shall not find salvation, for he has slipped away, and fallen into grievous sin, because he has not admonished, nor converted those who have committed many sins, but has scattered the flock of God, and also fought against Him. For God is righteous, and righteous is His judgment, with which He judges all, righteous men and sinners; (He is} merciful to those who turn to Him in righteousness and mercy and meekness, as David the beloved of God (says).

The bishop, then, ought to judge upright and follow after God and do His will, for ident righteously those that turn to Him. Remember you not David, when he sinned and Nathan said to him, Why have you done thus? And he said, I have sinned and I repent. And when he confessed his iniquity, he was saved from death. And Nathan said to him, “Be of good cheer and doubt not; you shall not die.” Jonah the prophet, also, not wishing to preach to the men of Nineveh, was plunged in the sea, and a whale swallowed him up, but afterwards he came forth from the whale’s belly, and was saved from death. And Hezekiah, also, when he became proud, judgment came upon him. And Hezekiah humbled himself, and forsook his pride, and wept before God, and (God) had mercy on him. Hear, you bishops, the profit that is in this matter; for it is written in the Fourth Book of Kings: ‘And Manasseh his son reigned in his stead. Twelve years old was Manasseh when he began to reign, (and) fifty and five years reigned he in Jerusalem, and his mother’s name was Hephzibah; and he did evil in the sight of the Lord.” Moreover it is written in the Second Book of Chronicles, saying, “And he did evil in the sight of the Lord more than all the uncleanness of the nations whom the Lord rooted out from before the children of Israel. And he turned and built in the high place the altar which Hezekiah his father had destroyed, and he set up pillars for the Baalim, and made groves, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them. And he built an altar in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord said,!! And he built altars for all the stars of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord; and he himself made his own sons to pass through the fire in the land of Benomnimén," and used signs, and (made himself like an ass and practised magic, and set up diviners and soothsayers, (and) wrought much evil in the sight of the Lord to sin against Him. And he set the graven and molten images which he made in the house of the Lord; (of which the Lord had said) to David and Solomon his son, In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, will I set my name for ever; and I will not again move the foot of Israel from the land which I gave to their fathers. However let them observe all that I have commanded them in all my law and my ordinances and my judgments by the hand of Moses. And Manasseh made Judah to sin, and them that dwelt in Jerusalem, by doing evil above all the nations whom the Lord removed before the face of the children of Israel. And the Lord spoke against Manasseh and against his people, and they hearkened not to him. And the Lord sent against them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, and they took Manasseh in bonds, and bound him in chains, and brought him to Babylon. Terrible is the plague of your wrath against sinners. The mercy of your commandment has no number, nor measure, for you alone are the Lord most high, merciful, slow of anger, and bountiful in compassion, and gentle towards the sins of the sons of men. And now, O my Lord, the God of the righteous, for it is not for a righteous man that you have appointed repentance, not for Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, who sinned not against you, turn you to the repentance of mea sinner, for I have sinned beyond the number of the sand of the sea; and my sins are many. And I am not worthy to look up, and behold the height of heaven, because of the multitude of my iniquities. I have toiled in chains of iron, that I might get me respite of my sins, and by this also I have had no respite, for I have provoked you to anger, and done evil in your sight, observing vanities and multiplying things that profited me not. And now I bow the knees of my heart, entreating your mercy. I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned; and I confess my sin. I make supplication and entreat of you; have compassion on me, O Lord, have compassion on me, and deliver me not over to my sin. Reserve not evil against me for ever; and take not vengeance upon me in the depths of the earth. For you, O Lord, art the God of those that repent; and your goodness shall be manifest upon me, since while I was not worthy, you did save me in the multitude of your compassion. I will glorify you at all times and all the days of my life; for all the host of heaven glorify you, and yours is the glory for ever. Amen.”

And when the Lord saw that Manasseh repented of the evil Of his doings which he had done in his ignorance, the Lord pardoned him and heard his prayer and accepted the voice of his petition. And at once a flame of fire encircled him, and the bonds of his chains of iron were loosed. Then the Lord saved Manasseh from all his affliction, “and brought him back to Jerusalem to his kingdom. And Manasseh knew that the Lord was his God,” and he served the Lord with all his heart and with all his soul, all the days of his life; and he was reckoned with the righteous. Then he thrust forth from the house of the Lord the strange gods that were made by the hands of men, “and he raised high (the wall),? and appointed captains of the host in every place over the walls of Judah. And all the altars which he had built on the mountain of the house of the Lord and in Jerusalem, he utterly destroyed from out the city; and he erected the altar of the Lord, and sacrificed on the altar,?> and offered praise. And Manasseh spoke to Judah to serve the Lord, the God of Israel. And Manasseh slept with his fathers in peace; and Amon” his son reigned in his stead. And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, as Manasseh his father had done, and provoked the Lord his God to anger.’” Behold then, you have heard, our children, how he served idols, and sacrificed to them, and in his lawlessness slew many. And the Lord God afflicted him for a while, but when he repented, He forgave his sins, and restored him to his kingdom. For God receives the repentance of them that turn to Him, and restores them again to their former honour. For there is no sin greater than idolatry, since it is rebellion against God, yet men are saved from it by true repentance. But whosoever transgress and commits sin, and says in his heart,? What will God do to me?, he is a rebel against God. For he does not first try himself, but walks in his own way, and does the desire of his soul, and says, This is good. Whoever does thus, and repents not, shall not have forgiveness. Thus, then, did Amon, the son of Manasseh. For the Holy Scripture says, Amon conceived rebellion in his heart, and did evil in the sight of the Lord, as Manasseh his father had done; and he multiplied proud words, and said, My father sinned much in his youth, and when he was old, he turned and repented. I also will do in like manner and will walk in mine own way, and will follow the desire of my soul, and when I am old, I will turn theréfrom,>? and repent before the Lord. Then Amon did evil in the sight of the Lord, and wrought exceeding much evil, as those before him had done. Then the Lord chastised him, and destroyed him from off the good land, and his servants [aid (hands) upon him, and slew him in (his) house. “And the people of the land slew those who had laid (hands) on King Amon. And he reigned two years.” Understand then, you people, and think not to do evil as Amon did, lest you be destroyed. In like manner, the bishop ought to feed and convert the people and admonish them, and heal them of their sickness and receive their repentance, so far as he is able. But if he be lacking in mercy, and receive not the repentance of sinners who turn to him,‘ he is despised and dishonoured, and shall be condemned before the Lord his God. But if he receive the repentance of those that turn to him,‘! he shall find compassion and mercy with the Lord God, who sent His only-begotten Son into the world; and He was pleased to be born of a woman, and was made man for our sakes. And He endured suffering on the Cross, and was wounded, and died. He is God the Word, the Angel of His great and terrible counsel; He took our sicknesses and bare our sufferings, and by His wounds our wounds have been healed..In like manner, let us, too, patiently endure suffering and affliction, and receive the repentance of them that have sinned.

See then the mercy of the Lord towards Matthew, who was a tax collector, when he turned to Him, He made him an evangelist; and towards Peter, who denied Him thrice through fear, when he repented and wept bitterly, He received his repentance, and made him the shepherd of His sheep; and towards Paul, our brother, though he was formerly a persecutor, who blasphemed against the Holy Spirit, yet when he turned to Him, He made him an apostle. And to the woman who was a sinner, who gave alms‘ to many, He said, Your sin has been forgiven you.” And the other woman also, the adulteress whom the priests set before Him to prove Him,‘ He saved, and said to her, “Go your way, from henceforth sin no more.” It is right for you, you bishops, to set your trust and hope in God, our Lord and our Saviour,‘ Jesus Christ the Saviour of your souls. Draw near to Him in meekness and in mercy, as peacemakers without strife and anger: convert the sinful, and lift up the fallen; and render not evil for evil. Moreover be you not rail ers, nor passionate, nor blasphemers, nor boastful, nor acceptors of persons, nor drinkers of much wine, nor drunkards, nor singers, nor dancers, nor thieves, nor murderers, nor takers of bribes. Neither seek. you honour and riches from strange gods, but keep far from them, for you have been called to this work, that you should serve God.:
Thus let the life of the bishop be. (Let)

his raiment and his food (be) in moderation and purity, as much as is sufficient for him, that he transgress not in any other way or matter. For he that serves is worthy of his food, even the tithes and first fruits which men bring to the Church, as is commanded by our Lord. The bishop may give what they need to the poor, and the needy, and the widows, and the orphans, and to the destitute, and to the strangers, and to them that have nothing. But if the bishop exercise no care for them, God will require it of him on their behalf, for (the bishop) has authority to appoint for every man, as is meet. And you also that are set in authority in the Church, if you have need, take from its store, but if you are not impoverished, it is not right that you should take therefrom. And if you act thus, you shall be saved before God. But if the bishops take for themselves alone, and be insatiable in eating, and lay up store for themselves, and give not to the destitute, God will require this of them, and they shall be clothed with shame and dishonour. Wherefore it is said, “You have drunk the milk, and clothed you with the wool, and have slain the bulls; you have not lifted up that which was fallen, nor helped that which was lost.” “Will you live alone upon the earth? Therefore has He commanded you in the law, saying, “Love your neighbour, as yourselves.” And moreover it is said, “You shall not muzzle the mouth of the ox when you tread out your grain.” And seek you not to take anything but that which is according to your service and your toil, as is right. For the threshing-floor is the Holy Church of God. And do you also eat therein, as the Levites, who served in the tabernacle of the testimony, which is a type of the Holy Church. It is meet, then, that the priests eat the offerings with their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, from the offering that has been offered to the Lord of Hosts, first-fruits, or tithes,) or a sacrifice, or an oblation; for they have no other duty, nor any portion of land with the children of Israel, but only to serve in the tabernacle; for the offering which the people bring is the portion of the Levites. And now you, O bishops, are the exemplars of the priests and Levites, as those of old. You ought to entreat and pray on behalf of the people, for you are prepared for the service of this church, who stand before the altars of the Lord our God, and (who) offer up a pure and reasonable and bloodless sacrifice to Jesus Christ, the great High-priest. Tor you are preachers,' and elders, and prophets, and rulers, and king's, who have authority over all the people and over all who are under you. It you to preach and speak and cause the people to hear the word of God, and not to ‘hide the keys of wisdom and knowledge. And if you hide them, you shall meet with condemnation, which is prepared for you before God; but if you preach and teach the people, you shall meet with honour and recompense before God, because you have patiently endured and borne every burden. Wherefore you shall attain in every thing that which you need,’ because you have imitated Jesus Christ, who took our sicknesses, and bare our sorrows on the Cross. For He, who had no sin, was crucified for us; in like manner you also must needs bear the sins of His people. For Isaiah the prophet says, concerning our Saviour, “He took our sicknesses and bare our sorrows, and for our sakes He was afflicted.” And again he says, ‘He was wounded for our sakes and for our sins, and was afflicted for our iniquities.”

should you also save the people, even as Christ saved you." Think not that the burden is light which presbyters and bishops bear. As they have borne a heavy burden, so they shall receive the first-fruits, and give thereof to the destitute.” For One will call you to account, with whom none can dispute or contend. It is right, then, that they who serve the Holy Church should have their needs supplied, and receive the offerings as priests, and Levites, and ministers; even as it is written in the Book of Numbers concerning the priests: “And the Lord said to Aaron, Behold, I have given to you to keep the first-fruits which they offer to me of all that is sanctified by the children of Israel; to you I have given it; (even all the first-fruits of grain that are in all their land and all that they offer to the Lord; to you have I given it all] until your old age,’ and after you to your children as an ordinance for ever. And this shall be yours of that which is sanctified to the holy place, of the sacrifices, both of every oblation, and of all their sacrifices, and of their trespass-offerings, and of all their sin-offerings; whatsoever they bring to me of all their holy things, to you shall it be and to your children. In the most holy place eat of it; let every male eat of it, you and your sons; for it is holy to you. And let this be yours of their first gifts, and of all that the children of Israel offer; to you have I given it, and to your sons and your daughters with you as an ordinance for ever. Let everyone that is clean in your house eat of it. And all the first-fruits of oil, and all the first-fruits of wine and wheat, even their first-fruits, and all that they offer to the Lord, to you I have given it. All the first-fruits of grain that are in all their land, and all that they offer to the Lord, to you have I given it all. Let him that is clean in your house eat of it. All that they dedicate among the children of Israel is yours, and everything that opens the womb of his mother of all flesh, everything that they bring to the Lord from man even to beast is yours. And those that are redeemed with a ransom, the first born of men, and the first born of beasts that are unclean, you shall redeem. And for a ransom for each one that is a month old, the price shall be fifty shekels according to the shekel of the sanctuary, (that) is twenty But the first born of cows and the first born of sheep and the first born of goats, you shall not redeem, for they are holy; and you shall pour out their blood at the altar, and their fat you shall make a sacrifice to the Lord for a sweet savour. And its flesh shall be for you; even as the breast which they offer, and as the right shoulder, it shall be yours. Every offering which is holy, even all that the children of Israel separate to the Lord, I have given it to your sons and your daughters with you as an ordinance for ever; and it is a perpetual decree for ever before the Lord to you and to your seed after you.”

Hear now also, you people of the elect Church of God. For of old the Hebrews were called the people of God, a holy people; but now you are priests, children of the Most High.” Speak no evil word against the gods, that is, the bishops; but let the bishops have the first seat amongst you, for to them has been given honour and glory from the Lord God, that they may feed His people in peace, as Christ the great High-priest." But let the deacon minister in purity without blame, and let him do nothing without the permission of the bishop his father. And let the deaconess do nothing without the permission of the deacon. And Ict no other woman go to the deacon save only with the deaconess; and in like manner let no woman go to the bishop save with the deacon. Honour then the priests, for they admonish you and teach you the way of God; and you shall receive from them the word in the right faith. Honour widows and orphans as the Church; and virgins also as the altar and the offering of incense.

For of old none was able to offer sacrifice except he were of the sons of Levi, and the people could not approach the altar except along with the priests.' And in like manner do you also do nothing without the counsel of the bishop. He who acts thus without the permission of the bishop his work is idle and vain and without profit. As Saul offered a sacrifice without Samuel the prophet, and heard a voice saying, “Your sacrifice is vain”; in like manner, if a layman do (anything) without the priest, it is vain. Uzziah the King also, when he was not a priest, and yet did the office of a priest, became a leper. And if there be anyone of the people that usurps the priest’s office, and does not the commandments of God, he shall not escape judgment, for he has taken an honour that was not given to him, and has resisted the priesthood, and has not imitated Christ, “who glorified not Himself to be made a great High-priest”; but patiently endured until He heard the voice of the Father saying, “The Lord swore, and will not repent, you are his priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.” But if Christ glorified not Himself without the Father who is equal with Him, how then can a man by himself take the priesthood to himself, unless he that has authority over him have given it to him? For the sons of Korah were of the tribe of Levi, yet when they strove against Moses and Aaron, the fire consumed them, because they sought to take that which belonged not to them. Dathan and Abi ram went down alive into Sheol. The rod that budded destroyed the counsel of many foolish men, and He made manifest thereby the great High-priest who was ordained by God. Therefore, brethren, you ought to bring your sacrifices and your incense to the bishop, for he is the High-priest. Bring to him your first-fruits and tithes (and) all your vows, that he may give to each one according to his need, even to the destitute who have nothing. Let him appoint to them as is fitting, that none wrong his neighbour in receiving alms. The bishop ought to exercise due care concerning all the destitute, and to examine their lives and know well their condition. Moreover when the faithful desire to invite to a feast the destitute and the widows, as the Lord has commanded, the deacons ought to minister. And let them, knowing well the lives (of all), invite them and set them each one in his place, as is fitting. And let them distribute to them; and to the shepherd also let them give thereof in secret, for the honour of God, seeing that the priesthood has been given to him. And after distribution has been made to the widows, let the deacons take thereof two portions; and in like manner the presbyters also, who watch, and teach the word of admonition, and let them receive double,?’ for they are apostles of our Lord, they being counsellors of the bishop, and the crown of the Church, who therein judge up rightly. And let the reader receive one portion, and in like manner the singers also, and let the door keepers get each one according to the appointment of the Church; and to the people let them give such portions as befit them.? And let them not neglect the bishop, nor delay to give to him, but send speedily to him along with the ministering deacons. The deacons ought to inform the bishop of every need of the people, that he may command them to do as befits. For of old there was no man that entered into the temple, or did anything (therein) without the priest. Malachi the prophet says, “For the priest’s lips keep counsel and search out the law.” For those who serve (false) gods, and do their will, and set themselves up. as righteous, though they are impure and their works evil, and (who) have no good works, and account themselves as the saints, men indeed seeing their works mock at, and detest, and despise them, yet is there none of these that can accomplish or do anything without the counsel of the idol-priests, but: they look up to them and hearken to the voice of him that commands them, and do all that he says to them; and they honour the idol-priests, and put their trust in them, and believe in their gods. Now if they believe in these that have no life, and (if they) serve unclean spirits in whom is no profit, and hope in vanity and set themselves up as righteous, how much more should we, who have received grace, and have an enlightened faith and a perfect hope wherein is no deceit, believe the message which is full of glory and without fear, that we may please the Lord our God. For know of a truth that the first fathers and the bishops are the mouth of God.

For Aaron spoke to Pharaoh, being a helper to Moses, and therefore he was called the prophet, and Moses was called the god of Pharaoh, as a king and high-priest. Even as God said to him, “Behold, I have made you to be a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother to be to you a prophet.” How then do you not believe them, for they intercede for you, and deliver the word?

Serve them, for they are prophets and servants of God, the deacon like Aaron, and the bishop like Moses. And if Moses was called a god by the Lord, it is right that for you also to honour the bishops as God, and the deacon as a prophet. As Christ did nothing without the Father, in like manner let the lea con do nothing without the counsel of the bishop. Also there is nothing that the Son does without the Father, and as the Son is subject to His Father, in like manner let the deacon be subject to the bishop.

Even as the Son is the good pleasure of the Father, and His angel of counsel and His prophet, in like manner is the deacon the messenger and prophet of do anything without the counsel of the bishop.
