And because of this we all have assembled in one place, we are the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ, Peter and Andrew; James and John, the sons of Zebedee; Philip and Bartholomew; Matthew and Thomas; James the son of Alphzus and Simon the Cananean; ‘Thaddeus and Matthias who was numbered with us and appointed in place of Judas Iscariot; and James the brother of our Lord Jesus Christ, the bishop of Jerusalem and Paul the chosen (vessel) and teacher of the Gentiles, and being gathered together in one place we have sent to you this holy message.” You also, faithful brethren, have believed in Christ, by whom were all things: and now also we say to you that there is One God Almighty, and there is no other god besides Him; (and) we teach you to worship Him, and adore Him, and to serve Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit, and to read the Holy Scriptures of the Law and the prophets. Honour your parents, and abstain from all that contends against the law; and believe in the resurrection and the day of judgment; and wait in hope for that time. when He shall render to every man according to his works.

For the whole creation is from God, and not from Satan; but all evil is from Satan. And in lawful marriage there is no defilement nor loss, but rather it is from God, for in the beginning He created (them) male and female; and for this cause it is said “Let a man leave his father and his mother, and cleave to his wife, and let them two be one flesh.” And after a man is married, let him not put away his wife, but for fornication only, for ‘she is your spirit and your flesh, for I created them and not another.” Again, it is said, “What God has joined together let not man separate.” For he that separates himself from his wife, dividing the one flesh, has transgressed the commandment of God. He also that has married one that is divorced has defiled his flesh; and he that has cleaved to an adulteress has quite transgressed the law. Cut off the adulteress from your flesh, for she is not yours. Defile you not then your flesh, for circumcision of the heart in a pure spirit is sufficient for the faithful.

Make no repetition of baptism: the first baptism which you have received suffices for you, for you were buried into the death of Christ; (a baptism) which has not been given to the ungodly and unbelieving, but to holy priests who have bestowed it upon you into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Receive not baptism at the hands of apostates from the faith. For there is one baptism, and one God, the Father, and our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, and the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit: one is the death of Jesus in the flesh; and in like manner let your baptism which you have received into His death be one. And he that believes not, and does not thus, his portion shall be with the ungodly in their evil doctrine.

you have rejected my doctrine, also will reject you and forsake you, and not make you priests to me. And those who are baptized by them are not cleansed, but are unclean, and have no remission of sin. So are they who receive a second baptism, and make the work of Christ a mockery, and despise holy things, and blaspheme against the Holy Spirit, and count unclean His precious blood, and made light of His sufferings and His testimony. But those who believe not, and are not baptized into the right faith, are transgressors of the law and condemned, for they reproach Him, and give Him not thanks. Delay not to turn to the Lord for man knows not that which shall come upon him. And baptize your children, while they are babes, and feed them with spiritual food, and bring them up with admonition and wisdom, for it is said, Suffer the little children (and) forbid them not to come to me.” Behold we have written all this to you, beloved brethren, that you may understand wisdom and knowledge, and not receive idle words which the ungodly put forth in our name. Say not, then, We have apostles who will pray for us, but rather see whether their deeds are right. From those who do thus keep far away, lest you be condemned with those that have written to lead astray the faithful, who are blameless, the disciples of our Lord Jesus Christ.

We said, then, concerning bishops and presbyters that they should live with one wife before ordination, but that after ordination it is net right that they should marry. And again we give commandment concerning the servants who are obedient to the Church, sub-deacons, and readers, and door keepers that they should live with one wife, and (in one) marriage. But after they have received baptism and ordination, let them not commit sin, lest they fall into condemnation. Behold we give commandment that they marry not a harlot, nor a servant, nor a woman that is divorced, nor a widow, even as it is written in the law. Moreover let the deaconess be a pure virgin, or a faithful widow who has been married to one man. (Such) women ought to be appointed.

Those women also who turn from sin, receive. This is the will of God in Jesus Christ. And as touching the catechumens when they understand the teaching, baptize them into the name to the Father, These words come in awkwardly here.

… and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit; and command the faithful to separate themselves from those that serve not God, (and not to have fellowship with them) in anything, whether counsel or word or prayer. And put them forth from the Church of God, for they are strangers, and evil, and corrupt, who destroy the sheep of Christ's flock; concerning whom the wise Solomon says, Woe to the unbelieving who account themselves wise, and their latter end (comes) to the condemnation of Sheol.” These are they that teach false doctrine, and blaspheme against the Holy Spirit, from whom has been taken the portion of the inheritance which they received from Him, and who have forgiveness neither in this world, nor in that which is to come. For they have transgressed more grievously than the Jews and the heathen, who have blasphemed against God (who is) the Creator of all things and is above all; and they have risen up against His Son, and denied the Holy Spirit, and made void the holy Scriptures, and made blasphemy their portion,” and spoiled the Church of Christ. These are the foxes that spoil the vineyard. From such we bid you keep far away. For he that follows a wise man shall be wise like to him; but he that follows a fool shall be a fool like to him. You ought not to dwell with robbers, nor be partakers with adulterers. Hear what the holy David says, “I have hated, O Lord, them that hate you, and have been troubled because of your enemies. I have hated them with a perfect hatred and they are become my enemies.” For God cursed Jehoshaphat because of the love and help of King Ahab; and to King [Uzziah] he said by [Joel] the prophet, “You have been a help to a sinner; will you then save him whom the Lord has hated?” Wherefore there came on him speedily the anger of the Lord; because his heart was not right with Him, his works were diminished in the earth. Keep, then, far from them, and receive not ‘their salutation. Concerning them says the prophet, ‘The wicked have no rejoicing before God.” These are ravening wolves and dogs that have no mercy. And when the day has drawn near and the hour is come, they will be evil, even as our Lord says in the Gospel, “In the latter days faith and love shall grow less, and sin shall be multiplied, and there shall come false Christs and false prophets, and they shall do signs in heaven and seduce many of the elect.’ Behold then let us pray to God to save us from their error by Jesus Christ, and to deliver us from the ungodly people, that we may confirm the Church and save many, and heal them by much admonition, and by the word of grace. But those who received not our preaching could not be healed, and have gone forth from the flock, lest they should corrupt other undefiled sheep in whom was no blemish. Thus, then, we have ordained in all lands, and have set forth for you this right doctrine of the Didascalia in truth and in purity, as a memorial for those who believed in our Lord Jesus Christ; and we have sent (it) with Clement the beloved and the elect Barnabas, and our beloved son Timothy, and the blessed Mark, and with these Titus and Luke, and Jason and Lucius, and Sosipater.

We beseech you therefore: imitate these, and hear their words, and shun your former manner of life, for the former things have passed away; and become new yourselves, for you have known our Lord Jesus Christ by whom are all things; and (who) has given to us a pure law (for) the salvation of our souls, wherein He put His own perfect name, which is without division or defect, or change, unspotted and converting souls. When the Hebrews forgot this, He gave them a memorial by Malachi the prophet, who says, ‘Remember the law of Moses the man of God who enjoined on you these commandments of righteousness and holiness.” But our Lord Jesus Christ did not abolish the ordinances of the Law, nor diminish (them), but rather said, One word shall not pass from the Law, till all this be fulfilled.” Again, He says, “I have not come to abolish the Law and the prophets, but to fulfil them.” or Moses the legislator, prophet and king, and Elijah the prophet, who appeared with our Lord when He was transfigured before them, bare testimony concerning His passion and His death and His incarnation as friends, and men of His household, and not as strangers.

‘he Lord gave the ordinance, the ten words which are in the Law and the holy prophets, and they heard His voice continuously, before they made for themselves the calf which the Egyptians called Apis For the ordinance is righteous, and therefore vas it called the law; and He judges in uprightness. Simon and those with him hate this ordinance, and praise themselves, but they shall go down to Gehenna. But the law is good and holy, for He says, “If you will make for me an altar, build it for me in the land,” and He says not, “Build for me,” except \(it be) your pleasure, for God needs not sacrifices and offerings from us. But Abel, and Noah, and Abraham, the friends of God, offered up sacrifices of incense to Him according to their pleasure. And in like manner the Hebrews did thus according to their pleasure. And it was not He who commanded them, but they themselves did His good pleasure, and He received their sacrifices which they offered up to Him with a pure heart. Wherefore He says, desire not your incense, nor do I need anything, for the world is mine and all that is therein.” In days of old the people forget God, and made for themselves a calf as a god instead of the true God. And abide you in this ordinance, and know that there is no other god besides Him in heaven or in earth; love Him with all your heart, and with all your strength, and with all your mind; and fear Him alone, and set not in your heart the name of strange gods, nor make mention of them with your mouth, for because of the guile of their hearts God bound them.

But as for you, since you have known the One God with a pure heart, and a good understanding, and have heard the voice of the Saviour, blessed are your eyes, for they have seen, and your ears for they have heard. Behold you are loosed from the bonds and are freed from the servitude. Moreover He says, will not call you my servants, for the servant knows not what his lord does to him; but you are my friends.

But blessed are you from whom God has taken away His curse. lor Christ the Son of God came, (and) established and fulfilled the law; and He removed the heavy burden that was therein, (and) saved us, and freed us from the service of sin, and had mercy on us, and gave us life eternal. And again He says, ‘He that will come after me, let him await my second coming.” But He received not the sacrifices and offerings which the nations offered, for oftentimes they offered to Him; and they thought that it was by multiplying sacrifices that they would be saved, without repentance, from the scourge of God's anger. Moreover it is said, Wherefore bring you to me incense from Saba, and cinnamon from a far country? I have no pleasure in your sacrifices, and will not receive. your incense.” And again Isaiah says, Wherefore offer you to me your sacrifices; I am sated with the sacrifices of rams and oxen and with the fat of sheep. I desire not the blood of oxen and goats. If you bring (them), will you not show me who has required this at your hands? You shall not again tread the courts of my house. And if you bring fine flour, it is in vain; your incense, and your feasts, and your sabbaths, and your great day I desire not; your fasts also and your prayers I desire not; my soul has hated (them) and you are an abomination to me.” Moreover the prophet says, “Remove from me the sound of your anger.” Again Samuel the prophet said to Saul, when he desired to sacrifice, “To hearken is better than to sacrifice and knowledge than the fat of sheep, for the Lord desires not that you should sacrifice to him, but rather that you should hearken to his word.” And David also says, “I will take no oxen from your house, nor rams from your flock, for all the beasts of the field are mine; the cattle of the field also, and the oxen; and I know all the birds of the heaven; and the beauty of field also is with me. If I be hungry I will not ask of you, for the whole world is mine, with the fulness thereof. will not eat the flesh of oxen, nor drink the blood of goats. Sacrifice to God the sacrifice of praise and send up your prayer to the Most High.” Moreover it is written in the Scripture that He desires not the incense of those that have sinned against Him, for unclean before Him is the sacrifice of the ungodly who offer contrary to the law: everyone who eats of it is unclean. But He desires above all a meek heart and a humble spirit which are better than sacrifice. Behold, then, He came to bring to an end the sacrifices of blood which they offered.

For He said in the Law, “The Lord your God is One”; again He said in the Gospel, “This is life eternal that they should know the One true God.” Moreover He said, “Love your neighbour as yourself"; (and) repeated (it in the Gospel) and said, “I have given you a commandment that you love one another, as I have loved you.” For thus He said (in the law) You shall not kill, but He has commanded us never to hate anyone. He who said You shall not commit adultery nor desire your neighbour’s wife, behold He has commanded (us not even to look upon a woman to lust after her) He said (then), You shall not steal, but He has commanded us to abstain from every evil deed, and to love our enemies. For He who said, You shall not render evil to him that does you injury, has commanded us to be at peace with all men; for mercy is better than those who desire vengeance … He said (then), “Honour your parents’; but He has commanded us to humble ourselves to all men. He put an end to circumcision, and He Himself fulfilled circumcision: and He fulfilled the hope for which the whole world was hoping. He who said, “Perform to the Lord your oath,” has commanded us not to swear by anything. Instead of sacrifices of blood He has given us a rational bloodless offering; and instead of sacrifices in one place, He has commanded us that our offering should be made in all the earth from the rising of the sun even to its setting.”... Moses says in the law, Read you the words which I have commanded you while you work, or while you sit, or while you stand, or while you walk in the way.” And David also says, ‘But the law of the Lord is his delight, and in his law he will meditate day and night.” And everywhere He has commanded that they should do that which (is written) in the law, and not transgress the ordinance. And again it is said, “Blessed are they that are pure in their way, and that walk in his ways, and seek him with all their heart.” Moreover it is said in the Gospel, Blessed are you, if you do this.”

For on account of this is the law manifest in righteousness, and all the world, (even) those who believe in our Lord, and have forsaken the worship of idols, and kept far from wickedness and received all that is good. And the Jews also, who have rejected the covenants, whose hearts were blinded, and (who) followed the way of those who said, ‘We have no king but Caesar,” and said again, “If we let this man alone, the Romans will come, (and) will take away our nation and our land,” prophesied against Him and said, “It is better for us to put one man to death, than that the nation perish.” (Yet) all nations have believed in Him, and the Romans have taken away their authority and all their ordinances; and therefore are they accursed because they have not been able to do His commandment. Moreover it is said, “Cursed is he that does not all the commandments which are written in the book of the law."

But we follow the way of Christ, that we may receive a blessing: and let us receive the law, and the prophets, and the holy Gospel; and turn aside from those that worship many gods, and let us keep far from the murderers of Christ, and from them that slew the prophets. These are the unbelieving Jews. And let us be humble and firm in faith in Christ the King who has authority over all things, and is the teacher of the law, and the guardian of the ordinances.

And there are others who say that Jesus Christ is above the whole creation, and glorify Him and say that He alone is the Father; and again they say that He is the Son and the Paraclete. Are not these then more impious than all? And there are others who say that the resurrection of the dead (is of) souls without bodies. To these He says, Depart into fire eternal. Keep far (from such men), beloved brethren, lest you be condemned together with them. [And those that watch the stars, and worship the host of heaven, and observe days and hours, as for such, will He accept their prayers, and be pleased with their offerings and will they read the holy Scriptures? These then are void of the Holy Spirit, which abides in the heart of the faithful. Solomon says concerning the saints, ‘Let them be prepared, if they sleep, to watch; if they sleep and awake, to be wise in truth and love.” For the Holy Spirit is not far from faithful Christian people from the day of their birth, until they die. Let a woman after her child-bearing remain in her separation seven days. But if she think in her heart, and say, How shall the Holy Spirit abide upon me, while I am unclean and if (her) faith grow weak, and she be without good works, the Holy Spirit will not abide upon her. For this matter is not a transgression of the law, but marriage, and the customary separation of women, and nocturnal pollutions hinder not the Holy Spirit. But with the ungodly and unbelieving who have transgressed the law and the ordinances, the Holy Spirit will not abide. And those that have not the Holy Spirit are the habitation of unclean (spirits): but upon those that have believed and (that) hope in His second coming the Holy Spirit abides. [Tor the Paraclete hats lies and every (evil) work; and the devil hats works of righteousness and goodness. And whosoever is baptized in faith is separated from the spirit of Satan, and is the habitation of the Holy Spirit: and he that does His will is filled with wisdom and knowledge, and the unclean spirit cannot come near to him. The unclean spirit loves such as are ungrateful, slothful, and sinners and sorcerers, for the devil by his want of gratitude fell from his throne, and was deprived of the glory of God. And he himself chose to be Satan rather than to be an archangel. Wherefore women ought to beware of every evil and vain thing, and be mindful of God, who created all things, and to follow His law, (and) not work the pleasure of the flesh, except only in lawful wedlock. Beware then of the counsel of evil men, and of union with them.

Wherefore separate yourselves, beloved brethren, from all the heathen who practise evil, and keep far from them; and count not as an abomination the flesh of men’s dead bodies. We believe that the dead shall live and rise again. And in like manner lawful marriage is not an abomination, for the union of man and woman is righteous (before God) who created man and woman, and blessed them, and said to them, “Increase and multiply, and fill the earth.” Behold we understand that from God are all these things; without Him was not anything. They that do such things shall not escape from punishment, for they defile pure marriage, and do what is unseemly and what is not commanded in the law; (but as) it is said, ‘They are joined one to another, man with man. But they work their own shame, and their iniquity shall return on their own heads.” [For the Scripture says, “If any man lies with a man as with a woman; they have wrought uncleanness, let both of them die the death and, “He that lies with a beast, let him die the death and, “He that commits adultery with his neighbour’s wife, let him die the death,” for it is a shame to Israel. The hire of a harlot, and the price of a dog they shall not offer in the house of the Lord.” This is what is forbidden in the law, but marriage is pure. And God blessed the union of man and woman. And Solomon also says, “The union of man and man is abominable before the Lord.” David says, “Let your wife be as a pleasant vine in the chamber of your house, and your children also as young olive plants at your table. She did not name his name, but said of him, My lord is old. And in like manner, you men, love your wives, for they are your members and sharers with you in the begetting of children. It is said, “Love the wife of your youth, as the hart loves the fountains of waters; for she is yours and is with you at all times, and is a member of yours.” For it is said, “Take heed to yourselves and forsake not your wives.” And as touching the lawful union of man and wife, when they rise from sleep let them not give heed to ceremonial washings, but rather take thought for prayer and supplication to God. But if a man lie with the wife of his neighbour, or defile himself with a harlot, and, when he rises, wash himself in the sea, and in all the waters of the rivers, he shall not be able to cleanse himself; but his portion shall be rather in eternal condemnation.
Take no heed then of laws relating to the flesh, for lawful marriage is not unclean; nor seek after the way of the Jews, nor use at all times (such ceremonial) washings, nor practise their customary

Gather yourselves together diligently in the church, and read the holy Scriptures over those righteous Christians who have fallen asleep, and your brethren the martyrs who have entered into rest in the faith of Christ; and celebrate for them the eucharist,’ (and) offer in the church His holy Body and precious Blood. And when you bring (them) to the church and to the tomb sing psalms over them, for (it is said,) “precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of the righteous.” (And again,) Return to your rest, O my soul, for the Lord is your help.” And again it is said, The remembrance of the righteous man is with praise”; and “their souls are in the hand of God; even if they sleep, they are not dead."" Our Saviour said to the Sadducees, ‘Concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what the Scripture says, I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. He is not then the God of the dead. He is the God of the living,” [and not all are living nor....j.? Elisha also in his death (raised) him that was slain in Syria; when the dead body touched him, it was raised. The righteous Joseph also touched the body of Jacob on the bier, and was not defiled. And Moses and Joshua the son of Nun, when they brought forth the bones of Joseph from the land of Egypt and touched his bones, were not defiled. And in like manner, you bishops and all the people, when you touch the dead bodies of those that have fallen asleep, count it not an abomination to carry their bones, for you shall not be defiled on account of them. Remove, then, from you, this practice, for it is a thing of folly. And as for you, be you adorned with wisdom and knowledge, that you may find life eternal, and a portion with the souls of the righteous in the Kingdom of heaven, in a place of rest through Jesus Christ our Saviour, who is able to open the ears of your hearts that you may hear the words of God which have instructed you in the Gospel by the admonition of our Lord Jesus Christ the Nazarene, who was crucified in the days of Pontius Pilate and Herod the King: He suffered, and died, and rose from the dead, and shall come again with glory and with great power; (and) shall raise the dead, and render to every man according to his works; and He ascended with great glory to His Father. And after He rose from the dead, we saw Him, and ate and drank and abode with Him forty days; and then He ascended into heaven, and sat on the right hand of the Father, the Almighty who sits on the Cherubim; concerning whom David says, “The Lord said to my Lord, Sit you on my right hand, until I bring your enemies under the footstool of your feet whom the blessed Stephen saw, and cried and said, ‘Behold I see the heaven opened, and the Son of Man sitting on the right hand of God”; who created the hosts of: angels; to whom be great glory and honour and thanksgiving and dominion with His Father and the Holy Spirit, now and for ever and ever. Amen.

Moses the prophet said plainly to the people, even to the people of Israel, ‘And behold show you plainly the way of death, and (the way of) life; choose life for yourselves, that you may live.” And Elijah the prophet said to the people, “How long halts your heart concerning the Lord, the Lord is One; seek Him.” Our Lord Jesus Christ said, “A servant cannot serve two masters; otherwise he will obey one, and disobey the other. You cannot then serve God and wealth. We have followed our Lord Jesus Christ, who has mercy on the whole world.

We say then that there are two ways, one of death, and one of life: separate and having no connection one with the other; one which leads to death, and one (which leads) to life. The first is the way of life concerning which the Law has spoken, and said, “Love the lord your God with all your heart, and with all your strength and with (all) your soul, besides whom there is no other god,” and, “love your neighbour as yourself,” and “what you desire not for yourself, that do not to your neighbour,” Bless them that curse you, and pray for them that oppress you,” and Love your enemies,” “What then is your reward, if you do good to them that do good to you?” Take heed then and hate no man. And again it is said, “You shall not hate any man, neither an Egyptian, nor an Edo mite for they are all creatures of God. Keep far from evil men and from the desires of this world. “And to him that strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other.” For David says, “If I have rendered a return to them that rendered evil to me, let your enemies cause me to fall naked.” And again it is said, ‘If any man compel you to go one mile, go (with him) twain”; and, “If any man take your coat, leave to him your cloak (also)"; and, “Prevent not him that takes your goods”; and, “Give to him that asks of you, and shut not your door against him that desires to borrow of you.” For God is merciful (and) a lover of men, and gives all things to him that asks of Him. And the Father ‘“‘makes the sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the sinful.” You ought to give to all men of the labour of your hands; and honour you the saints. For it is said, ‘You shall do no murder.” (Everyman) is your image and your likeness; and there is nothing worse than murder. And, “You shall not commit adultery,” nor separate (what is) your flesh, nor make two parts (thereof); for it is said, “They twain shall be one flesh,” and one spirit; and in form (only) are they separate; and ‘You shall not steal,” for when Achan the Israelite stole, they stoned him with stones, and he perished; and in like manner. Gehazi stole and lied and was clad with the leprosy of Naaman the Syrian; and Judas Iscariot also stole the purse of alms (from) which alms were given to the poor, and betrayed the Lord of Glory into the hands of the Jews, and then repented, and hanged himself, and his bowels gushed out, and he died; ‘Ananias and Sapphire his wife kept back part of the price of their possessions, and lied to the Holy Spirit, and died by (the sentence of) our beloved brother Peter the Apostle.

You shall not practise magic, nor use divination, nor consult wizards, for it is said, ‘You shall not trust in wizards.” And, You shall not kill a child by abortion, for it is the image and spirit of God. And, “You shall not covet the possessions of your brother, nor his wife, nor his servant, nor his maid, nor his ass, nor his ox.” Moreover, you shall never swear falsely, but if you swear, swear truly. And again it is said, “You shall not bear false witness,” for “he that speaks lies against the poor provokes his creator to anger.” And the way of evildoers leads to death. You shall not be of a double heart, or of a double tongue, for ‘the snare of a man is the word of his mouth,” and, “a talkative man shall not prosper upon earth.” And let not your words be idle, for everyone that speaks thoughtlessly shall be condemned. And, You shall not be rapacious, for it is said, “Woe to them that wrong their neighbours.”

And you shall not accept persons, nor be deceitful in heart, nor proud, for “God humbles the proud.” And, You shall not hate any man, nor curse your brother, nor do evil to him. And abstain from all evil, and be not passionate, nor envious, lest that befall you that befell Cain, and Saul, and Joab. For Cain slew Abel his brother, and God chose Abel and accepted his sacrifice; and Saul persecuted David, when he overcame Goliath the Philistine, (and) was envious of him because of the songs which the women sang; and Joab, also slew Abner the Israelite, and Amasa of Judah.
,And, You shall not be a for you have heard what befell those who murmured against Moses. Be meek like Moses and David, for the meék shall inherit the earth.
Be you therefore merciful, for they shall obtain mercy. Accept every toil that comes upon you, like Job and Lazarus, that you may receive a reward from God.
And honour him that teaches you the word of God, and be mindful of him day and night, for where instruction is, there God is.
And reconcile those who are at variance, and judge up rightly, for the judgment is the Lord’s.
And when you pray, be not of a double heart. Peter said, He said to me while I was on the sea, Wherefore do you doubt, and make for yourself a double heart?
And if you give alms to the poor, Doubt not; know you then who it is that will render the reward; is it not the Lord? Give, then, to everyone that asks of you that which he needs.

And forget not any of the commandments of the Lord; and confess your trespass before Him, and sin no more, that you may find (that which is) good before the Lord your God, for He desires not the death of a sinner, but that he should turn to repentance.
And honour your father and your mother; forsake not your brethren and your kinsmen.

You shall give thanks thus: We give thanks to You, Creator of all things, for the -of this chrism, and for this oil of immortality,’ which have agi to us by Jesus Christ Your Son. For Yours is the glory for ever and ever. Amen. And whosoever comes to you, and give thanks thus, receive him as a disciple “Of Chest: if there be anyone that teaches contrary to the law which was given to you by the Lord, receive him not, and let him not have fellowship with you in thanksgiving. Prove everyone that comes to you, and examine diligently his deeds, (and) appoint as is fitting for you have knowledge of those on the right hand and on the left. And judge between those who rule justly and (those who) rule unjustly; and to your neighbour that judges justly do good according to his doings; to him also that judges unjustly render according to his doing; and pray not with him, lest you be defiled together with him. And every prophet and teacher that comes to you and teaches truly is worthy of his food, as a good workman who serves his lord.
To the priests also give the first-fruits that they may bless your labours; and give all the tithes to the widows, and to the orphans, and to travellers, and to strangers.

And on the Sabbath day, which is (the day of) the resurrection of our Lord, gather you together in one place, and give thanks to God for all the good things that He has done for you in Christ, that your sacrifice may be perfect and acceptable before God, for it is said concerning the Church that they shall assemble therein, and offer up incense and sacrifice, (for) “I, says the Lord, am a great King upholding all the world, and my name is terrible in all the world, and (among) the Gentiles.”

Appoint for yourselves bishops, presbyters, and deacons, meek men and humble, who are chosen from the people, pure and tried in every good work; who desire not money, but rather teach the word of the Lord and the doctrine, and discern in uprightness the commandments of Christ... as father and lord.. in love without anger and impatience, with a humble heart and in meekness. Observe all this that you have been commanded of the Lord for the life of your souls. Let your loins be girt, and your lamps burning, and be you ready as men who wait for their Lord when he comes, whether at the first hour of the night, or at midnight, or at cock-crowing, or at break of day. The Lord will come at a time that you expect not. Blessed are those servants whom their Lord, when he comes, shall find so doing. Behold, He will gird Himself, and go about, and serve them. Pray then and work, lest death come upon you suddenly.

And when the glory of the Son of Man shall appear in heaven, and the archangel shall blow the trumpet, and the dead shall be raised, and our Lord shall come with His Saints in the clouds of heaven, and all the angels of His power with Him, then shall He sit on the throne of His Kingdom, and destroy the devil, the deceiver, and shall render to every man according to his works; and then shall the sinners go into eternal condemnation, but the righteous into life eternal, and (these) shall rejoice in the Kingdom of heaven through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Be you, then, ready that you may receive His good things. Let us pray and make supplication to Him, and say, O, our Saviour; Who art before the world (was), God of gods, the Almighty, One God, the Creator of every creature, the Lord of our holy fathers, who were without blame before You, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (Who art) merciful, and ready to forgive sins, faithful and kind, in compassion and mercy, from whom nothing is hidden, (but) all is open before You: in You the souls of the righteous trust, and in You the saints hope; (You are) the Father of them that are blameless, and hear the prayer of the pure in heart, and hearken to the supplication of them that are silent. Make Your favour, O Lord, to dwell on every creature, for You know that which the heart thinks before the thought (comes); and in all the ends of the world they offer up to You sacrifice and incense with prayer and thanksgiving; Who have appointed days that men may do righteousness, and the gate of whose mercy is open to everyone that seeks You, and have appointed laws and ordinances, and caused us to understand that the riches of this world are transitory and that the ornament of beauty abides not for ever, and that the might of the strong decays speedily. For our father Abraham was the first to walk in the way of righteousness, and You gave him honour and riches, and in faith he accomplished his life; and You said to him, “I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand of the sea”; and You gave Isaac to him; You did bless him and say to him, “I will be with your seed after you.” For we have known Christ in our father Jacob, whom You did send to the land of Egypt,’ and did say to him, Behold I will be with you, and will surely multiply your seed exceedingly.”' And in like manner You did say to Moses, Your holy and faithful servant at the bush, “I am from before the world (was), and my name shall be for ever”; and Your memorial also is for generations of generations; Who did bless the seed of Abraham that they might be blessed for ever.:

You did create man that he might be a rational (creature), and You did say in Your wisdom, ‘Let us make man in our image and in our likeness and You did set Adam to be ruler over all, and did give him life eternal. And when he transgressed Your commandment, You did put him forth from the garden, and did bring death on him. Then You did send Your only-begotten Son and did raise him from his fall, and did restore him to the garden of delight.

You, O Lord, alone are great, and powerful, dnd terrible, merciful and kind, the Almighty who doest wonders, and withdraw not ‘Your compassion from any of Your works or creatures, good and a lover of men, and dealing gently with sinners, and bringing them back in the multitude of Your mercy, and though we are not worthy to look up to You, nor raise our eyes to heaven, You in the greatness of Your power regard our humility. The heavens are supported by Your commandment, and by Your word the earth is established, for You, O Lord, art mighty, and the righteousness of Your judgment has filled the earth which You have created.

All the spiritual hosts of angels are a flame of fire, and the holy cherubim with six wings glorify You with a loud voice, and sing with a voice that is never silent, and say, Holy, holy, holy, Lord of Hosts, the holiness of Your glory [is perfect and] fills the heavens and the earth.” The (whole) number of these angels, thrones and authorities, dominions and principalities, and powers, the cherubim and seraphim cry and say, Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel, and blessed be this Church of the nations (which) is like to the host of heaven. Day and night with holy soul and perfect heart thus they sing, and say, “The Chariot. of God is ten thousand times ten thousand and thousands of thousands of them that glorify the Lord in the holy mount of Sinai.”” The heavens and all that is therein give humble thanks to You, for You have hung the heavens as a vault, and have laid the foundations of the earth, and established it on the waters; and You have separated darkness from light, and numbered the stars in their fulness, and called them all by their names. The whole creation declares Your greatness, and the trees of the field also You have made to grow. Wherefore the whole creation of mankind must needs offer up to You glory and thanksgiving, sacrifice and offering and incense through our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, Your only-begotten Son. You alone art Almighty, good, and loving mercy, and beneficent, for Yours is the glory and power for ever and ever. Amen. You are in heaven, and You are on earth, and You are in the sea; Who have gathered together the whole creation from the confines of the earth, and there is no end of Your greatness. For it is not we who have said this, but You did say, am the Lord God who am above the heavens,” and I am present in every place, and besides me there is no other god. True is Your word, and there is none that is like to You, the holy God, the Lord of the Saints, and the souls of all are in Your hand. You are worthy of glory and exaltation, Whose throne is unchangeable, and (Whose) strength decays not, and (Whose) greatness none can declare, and the excellence of (Whose) beauty is marvellous. There is none that dares to draw near to your habitation, and the knowledge of Your wisdom is without number. Your righteousness has no end, You need none to counsel You, nor seek any to help You; You have no beginning nor any end; Your kingdom pass not away, and there is none that can overcome Your power, and innumerable are the hosts of angels who minister to You. You are the Father of wisdom, and the maker of the whole creation, and the framer of the law. You destroy the ungodly, and reward the righteous. (You are) God the Father of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, the Lord of those who give Him humble thanks, in Whom is no falsehood;. Who take no bribe in judgment, Whose praises are innumerable. To You is due the honour, and glory, and worship which every rational soul sends up to You for ever and ever. Amen.

O Lord Almighty, who did create the world by Jesus Christ our Saviour, and did appoint the Sabbath, and rest thereon from all Your work, and have commanded us to rest (on it) from all the work of our hands, and to be ready to serve and do Your commandments; and have given us feast days (for) the joy of our souls; and that we should remember the skill of Your wisdom, that God the word was pleased to be born of a woman for our sakes, and appeared manifestly in this world and was baptized as man, though He was God, and endured patiently the sufferings of the Cross, died and rose from the dead in great might. Wherefore we keep as a feast the holy day of His resurrection, and honour the first day of the week, and give glory, and sing praise to Him who conquer death and gave light to the whole world, and has bestowed on us incorruptible honour and glory, and has gathered the scattered people, and made them to be one pure flock, and has blessed them, even as He blessed Israel. (It was) You, O Lord, who brought our fathers from the land of Egypt, and did deliver them from bitter bondage, and did save them from the sea, and from the labour of the brick-kiln, and did bring them forth from the power of Pharaoh and his hosts; and led them through the sea on dry ground, and did sustain them with all good things in the wilderness, and appoint for them the law of the ten words which You did utter with Your voice, and did write with Your hands, and did command them to rest on the Sabbath day, that they might give You humble thanks, and be safe from all evil; and did bind them with words of admonition, and gather them and bring them into the house of Your sanctuary. Wherefore He has commanded us to rest on every Sabbath day, because on the Sabbath day our Lord rested from all His work. Let us, then, seek after all His law, and give thanks to Him, and bless God for all the good things that He has bestowed on us, the sons of men. And greater than all these is (the day of) His holy resurrection which our Lord and Saviour and Creator, God the Word, has taught us (to observe), He who was begotten before the world was created, the Son of the Father, and (was born) of the Virgin Mary without human father: He suffered and was crucified and died in the days of Pontius Pilate; and rose from the dead on the day of the Christian Sabbath. Remember, O Lord, that which we offer to You on this day, the sacrifice, and the oblation, and the eucharist of Your holy peace,‘ this great portion which You have given to us, that we may offer that which is good to the greatness of Your power.

And You have fulfilled the prophecy, and have shown mercy to Zion, and have had compassion on Jerusalem, and have exalted the throne of David your servant amongst us by the birth of Christ, who was born of a virgin of his seed according to the flesh. Do You, O Lord, receive the prayer and supplication of Your people who call upon You in truth, even as You did receive the sacrifices of the righteous each in its own time: first of Abel, whose sacrifice You did respect and receive; of Noah when he was going forth from the Ark; of Abraham when he was going forth from the land of the Chaldees; of Isaac when he was going forth from the Well of the Oath; of Jacob in Bethlehem; and of Moses in the mount; and of Aaron in the wilderness; and of Joshua the son of Nun in Gilgal; and of Gideon on the rock; and of Manoah and his wife in the plain; and of Samson when he was before he transgressed; and of Jephthah in war; and of Barak and Deborah over Sisera; and of Samuel in Mizpeh; and of David in the field of Oman the Jebusite; and of Solomon in Gibeon and+ in Jerusalem; and of Elijah on Mount Carmel; and of Elisha at the fountains; and of Jehoshaphat in battle; and of Hezekiah in his sickness and concerning Sennacherib; and of Manasseh in the mount of the Chaldees after he had transgressed; and of Josiah in Pasa; and of Ezra when he was returning; and of Daniel in the den of lions; and of Jonah in the belly of the whale; and of the Three Children in the furnace of fire; and of Hannah in the tabernacle of testimony by the ark; and of Nehemiah when he was building the wall with Zerubbabel; and of Mattathias and his sons on the hilltop and of Joel in the blessing; now also in like manner receive the prayer and supplication of those who offer to You with knowledge through Jesus Christ., We give thanks to You for all things. You take not from us Your compassion and Your mercy, for You are merciful and full of compassion in all generations, Who did receive Enosh, and Enoch, and Noah, (and did help) in the days of Moses and Joshua, (and) the Judges, and in the days of Samuel and Elijah and the other prophets, and in the days of David and the other kings, and in the days of Esther and Mordecai, and in the days of Judith, and in the days of Judas Maccabzus and his brethren: receive us also in like manner in our days through Your Son Jesus Christ the Great High-priest, who has saved us from the sword and famine, and has fed us and satisfied us, and healed us from (our) sickness, and protected us from evil tongues.' To You we give thanks at all times through Jesus Christ, who has bestowed on us a sweet and articulate voice, and a tongue fair as the sound of an instrument, and has made us to discern between sweet and bitter, (and given us) eyes to see, and ears to hear, and noses to smell, and hands to handle with, and feet to walk; and these You have created from a tiny drop that is gathered in the womb; and You did bestow (on man therewith) a soul that shall not dic, and make him a rational being. And You did instruct him by Your law and adorn him by Your commandments; and after a while You did make him mortal and did. grant him a resurrection. How then shall man repay You for all this that You have done for him? Now also we must needs give You thanks and glorify You according to the measure of our power. Receive (us) that (our service) may be acceptable before You; and save us from the apostasy of the wicked whose gods are many, and deliver us from those who contend against Christ, and free us from the error of Satan, for You did send Christ Your beloved Son to become man, though He is God, and did cause the Paraclete to dwell in us, and did set the angels to bless us, and did put Satan to shame. Since You have created us and granted us life, preserve us, and give us sustenance, and turn us to repentance; for You are worthy of glory and worship for all that You have done for us through Your Son our Saviour Jesus Christ for ever and ever. Amen. Follow after this at all times, brethren; the Lord be with you on earth and in heaven and in the Kingdom of His Father, who sent Him to free us from deeds of sin, and the service of Satan, and (who) has given life to the sons of men, even to those that believe in the Lord pads the Creator, that those who believe in Christ may ive.
What thanks is it fitting that we should offer to God the Father through Jesus Christ? Behold we have told you before, and have taught you. Observe all this that you may find life eternal. Amen.

He that desires to be baptized must needs be taught the word of instruction, and be made to understand the knowledge of God the Father, and be instructed as to the incarnation of the only-begotten Son and the good pleasure of the Holy Spirit. Moreover let them tell him that God created the world and man upon it, and how God sent judgment on the wicked by the waters of the flood, and destroyed sinners with fire, and did magnify the saints in all generations. These are Seth, and Enosh, and Enoch, and Noah, and Abraham, and all those that were begotten of them, and Melchizedek, and Job, and Moses, and Joshua, and Caleb, and Phinehas the priest, and all the righteous according to their generations; and how God pitied and chose mankind, and rejected them not, but rather called them, and turned them at all times from error and from vanity to true knowledge, and brought them forth from the service of the adversary, and made them an army to do His commandments, and saved them from deadly error, and led them to life. All this then let him understand who desires to be baptized, and (then) let him receive baptism. And let him who lays hands upon him worship God the Father the maker of all things, who sent to us His only-begotten Son Jesus Christ to save mankind, from filthiness of flesh and soul, and to sanctify them according to the good pleasure of His goodness, and to lead them in the way, and to enlighten the eyes of their hearts, that they might understand His wondrous works, and learn His righteousness and be far from wickedness, and walk in the way of uprightness, that they may he worthy to be baptized as sons of Christ, in a hope that is full of grace and truth. But let them have understanding of wisdom and knowledge, and receive the works of righteousness, that they may enter into life. And after the thanksgiving let them be taught the incarnation of the Lord and His sufferings, and His resurrection from the dead, and His ascension into heaven.

And let the who desires to be baptized be taught to renounce Satan, and to believe in Christ, and to forsake his former habits, and to purify his heart from all evil and revenge and impurity and deceit. Then let them receive the holy mysteries. As a wise man who purges his field of thorns and thistles, and sows wheat therein, so you also in like manner must needs be separated from all impurity, and cleanse your hearts from evil, that you may be worthy to receive holy baptism. For thus our Lord taught us, saying, “Baptize all nations into the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.”

And again, let them command him that is baptized to say thus, I renounce you, Satan, and all your works, and alf your evil, and all your service, and all your angels and all your arts, and all your might.? And after the renunciation you shall confess, and say, I believe in Christ; and again, I believe in the One true God the Father of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, the Almighty and the Creator of all things, by whom are all things; and I am baptized into His only-begotten Son Jesus Christ, who was begotten before the world (was), by the wifi of the Father, by whom all things were made, both those in heaven and those in earth, both visible and invisible; and who came down from heaven in the latter days, and was incarnate of the Holy Virgin Mar and was born in purity; and (who) fulfilled the lay of His Father, and was crucified for us in the days of Pontius Pilate, and died, and abode in the heart of the earth three days and three nights, and rose from the dead and ascended into heaven in glory, and sat on the right hand of the Father; and (hoy shall come again at the last day to judge the living and the dead, of whose Kingdom there is no end. And I am baptized also into the Paraclete the Holy Spirit, who proceeds from the Father, and was strong through the Son, and dwelt in the holy patriarchs: and (who), again, was sent upon the apostles from the Father by our Lord Jesus Christ; and after the apostles He was sent and given to the faithful in Jesus Christ; and (I am.
baptized) into the apostolic Church for remission of sins, and for the Kingdom of heaven, and for ike Iie to come for ever.

And after he has made confession, let him draw near to the anointing of the holy oil which the priests have consecrated for the remission of sins and let the priest pray and make supplication to God, and say, May God the Father the Father of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, King of kings sanctify and purify this oil in the name of His only-begotten Son Jesus Christ; may it be a spiritual grace and power for the remission of sins; and a pledge for this baptism by the anointing of this holy oil, that (he that comes thereto) may be worthy. to keep Your commandments.

When the priest stands over the water, let him pray thus, saying, O Lord our God, the Almighty, Father of Your only-begotten Son our Lord Jesus Christ, I give You thanks for that you did send Your only-begotten Son, and He has saved the whole world, and He hears all who make supplication to Him, and proclaims concerning the Kingdom of heaven, and remission of sins, and the resurrection of the dead. I glorify You, and give You thanks, and praise You that You did patiently endure the sufferings of death on the cross for all; Who have given us baptism, which is the new birth. I glorify You, O God the Father, God alone, in the name of Jesus Christ, and the Holy Spirit that You the Doer of all wonders have not rejected mankind; Who did create Adam and set him in the garden, and when he transgressed Your commandment, You did put him forth from the garden by Your righteous judgment, but in Your manifold mercy You did not cast him off, but did send Your Son in the latter days to become man, and to endure suffering without sin. I pray to You and entreat You; look down from heaven upon this water, and sanctify it by Your power, that all they who are baptized thereby according to Christ’s command may be together with Him partakers in His crucifixion, and His death, and His resurrection, and His ascension into heaven, that You may save them from the death of sin, and that they may live in righteousness. And after this let him baptize into the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and anoint with the oil of balsam, and say:

O Lord God, the Lord of the whole Creation, Who have granted us the sweet savour of this chrism, even to all the nations who believe in You, (grant) also as a mystery to those that the efficacy of this chrism are baptized into Your name. And after this he shall stand, an Father who art in heaven,” to the end thereof. Then let the priest turn towards the East, and raise his eyes i
to heaven, and Say Glorify the Lord for the Lord Is good; and sing to His name, for it is i mercy is for ever.

The catechumens who have been baptized shall say this prayer: O God Almighty, the Father of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son, that love a body undefiled, and accept a meek heart and a humble spirit, and a knowledge of wisdom that has no decay, make Your Holy Spirit to dwell in us by Your good will and the strength of Your power through Jesus Christ, by whom to You be glory and power with Him and with the Holy Spirit for ever and ever. Amen.

These are the names of those who were ordained by us. First in Jerusalem, James, the brother of our Lord; and after him was ordained in his stead Simeon, the son of Cleo pas; and after him Judas the son of James. And in Caesarea of Palestine, first, Zaccheus the tax collector; and after him, Cornelius; and after him, Theophilus. And in Antioch, first, Evodius by Peter; and after him Iynatius, by Paul. And in Alexandria, first, Annianus, who was ordained by Mark the Evangelist; and after him, Avilius by Luke the Evangelist. And in the Church of Rome, first, Linus by Paul; and after him Clement, who was ordained by Peter. And in Ephesus, first, Timothy by Paul; and after him was ordained John by John the Evangelist. And in Smyrna, first, Aristos; and after him Strataeas, the son of Lois and after him Ariston. And in Pergamus, first, Gaius. And in Philadelphia, first, Demetrius by Peter. And in Cenchreae, first, Lucius by Paul. And in Crete, Titus. And in Athens, Dionysius. And in the three cities of Phoenicia, Marthones. And in Laodicea, Archippus. And in Colassae, Philemon. And in Macedonia and in Beroea, Onesimus (the servant) of Philemon. And in the Church of Galatia, Crescens. In the region of Asia, Aquila and Nice tas. And in the Church Aegina, Crispus.

These are they whom we entrusted (with the churches), and ordained in Jerusalem, and sent forth to preach and to teach in their several regions. Remember, then, their toil, and receive their admonition, and observe their words.
May the Lord be with you from henceforth and for ever, even as He said to us when He was ascending to heaven to the Father, ‘Behold I am with you all the days to the end of the world.”
Glory be to God, to whom be glory and honour for ever, and ever, and ever.
So be it. Amen and Amen. So be it.
Here ends the doctrine of the Didascalia of the fathers, the Apostles.
